introLines.speaker: NARRATOR
introLines.text: The twenty-eight days are over. There will be no royal wedding this season.

introLines.speaker: NARRATOR
introLines.text: No clever message, extra training session or well-timed browser refresh can bring the last day back.

introLines.speaker: PLAYER
introLines.text: “I’d like to appeal the deadline.”

introLines.speaker: NARRATOR
introLines.text: A clerk stamps your appeal *RECEIVED*, then stamps a second page *DENIED* without reading the first.

introLines.speaker: NARRATOR
introLines.text: The clerk hands back your journal. Every choice you made is still in it, and it stays yours until you restart or begin a new route.

introLines.speaker: NARRATOR
introLines.text: **Ending: The Courtship Window Closes.**

meta.Type: Terminal failure, shown following expiration of Day 28 without a successful marriage.
meta.END: Preserve terminal failed run and journal. No automatic restart. Offer separately confirmed Restart Current Route / Start New Route and read-only review access. Existing unlocked gallery endings remain intact. No playable Day 29.

introLines.speaker: NARRATOR
introLines.text: Last night, you were a software engineer reading rejection email number forty-one.

introLines.speaker: NARRATOR
introLines.text: It began with *Unfortunately*. They always begin with *Unfortunately*.

introLines.speaker: PLAYER
introLines.text: “I’m starting to think the job market was balanced by a game designer who hates me personally.”

introLines.speaker: NARRATOR
introLines.text: Then the world folded like a badly tested dropdown, and you fell out of it into a kingdom with more castles than entry-level openings.

introLines.speaker: NARRATOR
introLines.text: The first thing you see is a royal notice nailed to a wall: *THE COURTSHIP SEASON IS OPEN. TWENTY-EIGHT DAYS. ONE PRINCESS. GENUINE AFFECTION ONLY. NO EXTENSIONS.*

introLines.speaker: PLAYER
introLines.text: “I was hoping for a recruiter, but sure.”

introLines.speaker: NARRATOR
introLines.text: Underneath, in smaller letters: *Improve yourself. Learn her weekly schedule. Remember that the princess is allowed to say no.*

introLines.speaker: PLAYER
introLines.text: “Finally. An application process with clear requirements.”

introLines.speaker: NARRATOR
introLines.text: Day one begins. Somewhere in this kingdom, a princess is about to have a very unusual month.

meta.Type: Introductory, no time cost. Played after starting a newly named route, before the first regular gameplay action.
meta.END: No journaled gameplay action, stat reward, relationship gain, or time advancement; transitions to Day 1, morning. The 'courtship season' framing of the deadline is a **proposed new lore detail** requiring approval.

introLines.speaker: NARRATOR
introLines.text: The Palace Court has prepared a wedding with thirteen banners and nine trumpets that nobody will sound today.

introLines.speaker: NARRATOR
introLines.text: There is also a document stating that both parties agree of their own free will. Kaedra has read all of it.

introLines.speaker: KAEDRA
introLines.text: “The document is excellent. I propose we apply the trumpet policy to all future events.”

introLines.speaker: PLAYER
introLines.text: “They seem proud of the trumpets, though.”

introLines.speaker: KAEDRA
introLines.text: “The court is welcome to marry the trumpets.”

introLines.speaker: NARRATOR
introLines.text: A few guests laugh. The rest stare. They have spent years edging toward pillars around this princess. Nobody warned them she was funny.

introLines.speaker: HERALD
introLines.text: “Do you, Princess Kaedra, enter this partnership of your own free will?”

introLines.speaker: KAEDRA
introLines.text: “I do. I remain guardian of the people I serve, and I choose {PLAYER} as my partner.”

introLines.speaker: KAEDRA
introLines.text: “Neither my subject nor my keeper.”

introLines.speaker: HERALD
introLines.text: “And do you, {PLAYER}, choose Princess Kaedra of your own free will?”

introLines.speaker: PLAYER
introLines.text: “I do. Including the days she comes home from saving the kingdom and wants five minutes of silence.”

introLines.speaker: KAEDRA
introLines.text: “Ten minutes. I have negotiated the terms.”

introLines.speaker: NARRATOR
introLines.text: The court records the vows. Nine trumpeters go home without playing a note.

introLines.speaker: NARRATOR
introLines.text: Later, in the Royal Gardens, she sits close enough for your shoulders to touch. Nobody asks her to stand guard over anything.

introLines.speaker: KAEDRA
introLines.text: “There will still be frightening days. And days when I get things wrong.”

introLines.speaker: PLAYER
introLines.text: “Then we tell each other when we need help.”

introLines.speaker: KAEDRA
introLines.text: “Agreed. No document required.”

introLines.speaker: NARRATOR
introLines.text: She rests her forehead against yours. There is nobody here to see it.

introLines.speaker: KAEDRA
introLines.text: “For the record, our children will not study ceremonial speechwriting until they are old enough to refuse.”

introLines.speaker: PLAYER
introLines.text: “How many children is this policy for?”

introLines.speaker: KAEDRA
introLines.text: “I will not approve a figure before the relevant committee has met.”

introLines.speaker: PLAYER
introLines.text: “Who’s on the committee?”

introLines.speaker: KAEDRA
introLines.text: “You and I. The minutes will be brief.”

meta.Type: Free presentation after committed terminal success; safe to revisit via ending gallery.
meta.Eligibility: The Kaedra route is already successful and its completed-ending gallery entry is committed.
meta.Location: Existing **Palace Court**, with a quieter final moment beside the **Royal Gardens**. This is a narrated ceremonial transition **after victory**, no gameplay slot or new map location.
meta.Objective: Conclude Kaedra's willingness to be seen as powerful and tender, preserve her independent guardian responsibilities, and end with a restrained joke.
meta.END: Display-only epilogue. No gameplay cost, stats, heart changes, journal action, new gameplay permissions, or second gallery unlock. Future offspring are a playful hypothetical joke, **not canon-confirmed children or a child-count mechanic**. The source of truth remains the already committed successful route. The ceremony and garden ending do not add locations or actions.

introLines.speaker: NARRATOR
introLines.text: A young messenger is whispering urgently to an attendant. By the third listener, the story has grown two extra horns.

introLines.speaker: MESSENGER
introLines.text: “A monster near the royal paths! Great armored back! Enormous claws! An impossible stare! And the princess was *nearby*!”

introLines.speaker: KAEDRA
introLines.text: “I have the usual number of horns. Please keep that part accurate.”

introLines.speaker: PLAYER
introLines.text: “So what did people actually see?”

introLines.speaker: NARRATOR
introLines.text: A small, moss-backed creature trundles out from behind a step. A fallen blossom sits on its head like a crown.

introLines.speaker: NARRATOR
introLines.text: It is unarmed. It appears to be looking for shade.

introLines.speaker: KAEDRA
introLines.text: “Oh. There you are.”

introLines.speaker: MESSENGER
introLines.text: “You *know* it?”

introLines.speaker: KAEDRA
introLines.text: “It once stole a judge’s lunch and left the plate very clean.”

introLines.speaker: KAEDRA
introLines.text: “The court considers this political commentary.”

introLines.speaker: PLAYER
introLines.text: “Does it bite?”

introLines.speaker: KAEDRA
introLines.text: “Only unattended sandwiches.”

introLines.speaker: NARRATOR
introLines.text: The creature wanders toward a busy walkway. Kaedra asks people to give it room, then points it down the shaded route home. Nobody draws a weapon.

introLines.speaker: MESSENGER
introLines.text: “So… there was no monster attack?”

introLines.speaker: KAEDRA
introLines.text: “There was a rumor. Several people believed it enough to run. One of them ran into a door.”

introLines.speaker: KAEDRA
introLines.text: “The story was foolish. The door was very real. I take that part seriously.”

introLines.speaker: NARRATOR
introLines.text: Down the shaded path, the creature trundles out of sight. Kaedra notices you are still standing beside her.

options.labelText: “You calmed everyone down and got the little one home. Instead they made monsters out of you both.”

branchLines.speaker: KAEDRA
branchLines.text: “That is more or less what I was trying to do.”

branchLines.speaker: PLAYER
branchLines.text: “The sandwiches may disagree.”

branchLines.speaker: KAEDRA
branchLines.text: “Their concerns have been entered into the record.”

branchLines.speaker: NARRATOR
branchLines.text: She smiles. The messenger sees it and starts revising the rumor on the spot.

branchLines.speaker: KAEDRA
branchLines.text: “It helps that someone noticed.”

branchLines.speaker: NARRATOR
branchLines.text: Somewhere down the shaded path, a sandwich is left unattended for the last time.

options.labelText: “It’s a ridiculous rumor. Ignore it and it’ll blow over.”

branchLines.speaker: KAEDRA
branchLines.text: “It may. The bruise from the door will take longer.”

branchLines.speaker: PLAYER
branchLines.text: “I was trying to make it sound less serious.”

branchLines.speaker: KAEDRA
branchLines.text: “Please take me seriously. Just without turning me into a tragedy.”

branchLines.speaker: NARRATOR
branchLines.text: She goes to help the messenger straighten out the story. She does not ask you to come.

options.labelText: “Why reassure anyone? You’re frightening. So is that thing. Let them be scared.”

branchLines.speaker: KAEDRA
branchLines.text: “Fear is not a service I provide.”

branchLines.speaker: PLAYER
branchLines.text: “I didn’t think you’d take it personally.”

branchLines.speaker: KAEDRA
branchLines.text: “Then you have not been paying attention.”

branchLines.speaker: NARRATOR
branchLines.text: She walks the creature the rest of the way into the shade and does not come back.

meta.Type: Optional post-midpoint, once per run.
meta.Eligibility: Mandatory midpoint complete, Kindness ≥ 3, committed hearts below 10, no final retry pending, unused event flag, scheduled Kaedra slot/day, and no pending encounter. An already completed midpoint does not reset if later hearts drop below five.
meta.Location: Kaedra's scheduled Guild, Palace Court, or Royal Gardens location; a passerby and a small creature appear as scripted scenery, not new map nodes or combat content.
meta.Objective: Expose how rumors turn her into a monster and show that her protective response is gentle without making her a helpless victim or requiring the player to save her reputation.
meta.END: Mark this optional event experienced after first completed attempt, irrespective of branch. If **projected** hearts reach ten, immediately link `KAE-FIN-01` before committing the parent action.

introLines.speaker: NARRATOR
introLines.text: A prince has brought a traveling display of ceremonial cloaks. He is explaining, loudly, why a cape counts as an emergency public service.

introLines.speaker: PRINCE
introLines.text: “Every garment makes a statement. Mine says *behold my significance*.”

introLines.speaker: KAEDRA
introLines.text: “Mine says *someone forgot to account for door handles*.”

introLines.speaker: PLAYER
introLines.text: “That sounds like experience talking.”

introLines.speaker: KAEDRA
introLines.text: “I once turned around too quickly at a banquet. The curtains came down.”

introLines.speaker: KAEDRA
introLines.text: “Three ministers took it as a declaration of war. One of them surrendered.”

introLines.speaker: NARRATOR
introLines.text: The prince looks thrilled. Behind him, a guard begins inching toward a pillar.

introLines.speaker: PRINCE
introLines.text: “Princess Kaedra! Our most formidable guest! Will you model the silver mantle? And look *terrifying* in it?”

introLines.speaker: KAEDRA
introLines.text: “Is that a requirement of the mantle, or of me?”

introLines.speaker: PRINCE
introLines.text: “Whichever photographs better.”

introLines.speaker: NARRATOR
introLines.text: Several spectators wait for her to explode. She does not. A tailor drops a pin, and three of them flinch.

introLines.speaker: KAEDRA
introLines.text: “I was invited to assess whether the fasteners are safe. They are not.”

introLines.speaker: KAEDRA
introLines.text: “The mantle weighs about as much as a small door. All of it hangs from the collar.”

introLines.speaker: PLAYER
introLines.text: “And he wants you to model it anyway?”

introLines.speaker: KAEDRA
introLines.text: “He believes my face could frighten the stitching into cooperation.”

introLines.speaker: NARRATOR
introLines.text: She glances at you. The prince is already miming where the dramatic lighting would go.

options.labelText: “You’re here to inspect it, not haunt it. Want help making sure they hear about the collar?”

branchLines.speaker: KAEDRA
branchLines.text: “You heard the part about the collar.”

branchLines.speaker: PLAYER
branchLines.text: “And the curtains. But that’s a separate safety issue.”

branchLines.speaker: KAEDRA
branchLines.text: “Correct. We must not confuse the two departments.”

branchLines.speaker: NARRATOR
branchLines.text: Kaedra explains the clasp in four calm sentences. The tailor has it fixed before the prince finishes posing.

branchLines.speaker: PRINCE
branchLines.text: “Reinforced collars! The latest thing at court! I have always said so!”

branchLines.speaker: KAEDRA
branchLines.text: “I could have done that alone.”

branchLines.speaker: KAEDRA
branchLines.text: “It was easier with someone holding the door.”

options.labelText: “Oh, wear it. Do your legendary terrifying pose. It’d be hilarious.”

branchLines.speaker: KAEDRA
branchLines.text: “Hilarious for you.”

branchLines.speaker: PLAYER
branchLines.text: “I thought you liked jokes.”

branchLines.speaker: KAEDRA
branchLines.text: “I do. I like to be in on them.”

branchLines.speaker: NARRATOR
branchLines.text: She takes the loose clasp to the tailor herself. The prince photographs the mantle on its stand, looking formidable without her.

options.labelText: “Just threaten him. Scaring people is what you’re good at.”

branchLines.speaker: KAEDRA
branchLines.text: “No. I am good at making sure nobody has to be scared.”

branchLines.speaker: PLAYER
branchLines.text: “That’s not what I meant.”

branchLines.speaker: KAEDRA
branchLines.text: “It is what you said.”

branchLines.speaker: NARRATOR
branchLines.text: She turns back to the tailor. By the pillar, the guard stays exactly where he is.

meta.Type: Optional pre-midpoint, first completed attempt marks experienced whether successful or not.
meta.Eligibility: Kaedra route selected; milestone incomplete; committed hearts below 5; Strength ≥ 3; unused event flag; today's scheduled Kaedra slot and interaction unused; no pending encounter.

introLines.speaker: NARRATOR
introLines.text: The conversation should be ending. Kaedra stays.

introLines.speaker: KAEDRA
introLines.text: “You are remarkably difficult to intimidate, for someone who once called this kingdom’s job market a hostile deployment environment.”

introLines.speaker: PLAYER
introLines.text: “Still accurate.”

introLines.speaker: KAEDRA
introLines.text: “And yet you kept returning.”

introLines.speaker: NARRATOR
introLines.text: Her wings stay folded. Even her tail has gone still.

introLines.speaker: KAEDRA
introLines.text: “I want to say something before you assemble a ceremonial argument for why I am impressive.”

introLines.speaker: PLAYER
introLines.text: “Too late. I have three pages.”

introLines.speaker: KAEDRA
introLines.text: “Then there is still time to prevent a disaster.”

introLines.speaker: KAEDRA
introLines.text: “I like protecting people. I am not hoping someone will take it off my hands.”

introLines.speaker: KAEDRA
introLines.text: “But some days I come home tired. Some days I am unsure.”

introLines.speaker: KAEDRA
introLines.text: “I would like to say so without the room going silent.”

introLines.speaker: PLAYER
introLines.text: “Say it to me. I won’t go quiet.”

introLines.speaker: KAEDRA
introLines.text: “I have been called a weapon. And a guardian. And, in one very long speech, a legend.”

introLines.speaker: KAEDRA
introLines.text: “Given the choice, I would be someone’s equal. Someone you can argue with, and laugh with, and still trust to decide.”

introLines.speaker: NARRATOR
introLines.text: She reaches toward you and stops a hand’s width short. The answer matters too much to assume it.

introLines.speaker: KAEDRA
introLines.text: “I care for you. More than I’d planned to.”

introLines.speaker: KAEDRA
introLines.text: “You do not need to be fearless around me. I need you to see me clearly.”

introLines.speaker: PLAYER
introLines.text: “Kaedra…”

introLines.speaker: KAEDRA
introLines.text: “If this is a proposal, please do not begin with a list of my strengths. I have heard it. Usually with trumpets.”

introLines.speaker: NARRATOR
introLines.text: You leave the three pages in your pocket. One honest answer will have to do.

options.labelText: “No list. I love you strong, tired, and gentle when no one’s looking. Your choices stay yours. Marry me, and share an ordinary life as equals?”

branchLines.speaker: KAEDRA
branchLines.text: “An ordinary life?”

branchLines.speaker: PLAYER
branchLines.text: “Ordinary by this kingdom’s standards. There’ll still be royal speeches.”

branchLines.speaker: KAEDRA
branchLines.text: “Acceptable. If I may object to the page count.”

branchLines.speaker: NARRATOR
branchLines.text: She takes your hand. Her grip is firm, and loose enough to let go.

branchLines.speaker: KAEDRA
branchLines.text: “Yes, {PLAYER}.”

branchLines.speaker: KAEDRA
branchLines.text: “You do not need a guardian. I do not need a commander. I choose you anyway.”

branchLines.speaker: PLAYER
branchLines.text: “I can live with that.”

branchLines.speaker: KAEDRA
branchLines.text: “Good. Your proposal passed inspection.”

branchLines.speaker: KAEDRA
branchLines.text: “Barely.”

options.internalLabel: Correct; terminal success and gallery unlock; zero extra heart change

options.labelText: “You’re the greatest guardian who ever lived. I’d worship you every day. Marry me, and I’ll never question a thing you decide.”

branchLines.speaker: KAEDRA
branchLines.text: “Never?”

branchLines.speaker: PLAYER
branchLines.text: “Never.”

branchLines.speaker: KAEDRA
branchLines.text: “Then who will tell me when I am wrong?”

branchLines.speaker: KAEDRA
branchLines.text: “I have been admired since I was nine. Nobody doing it ever knew me.”

branchLines.speaker: NARRATOR
branchLines.text: She lowers the hand she had reached out with and says goodbye. It sounds provisional.

options.internalLabel: Incorrect; no heart penalty; later retry pending

options.labelText: “I’ll take over your duties and make sure you never make another mistake. Marry me, and you won’t have to be strong anymore.”

branchLines.speaker: KAEDRA
branchLines.text: “You have misunderstood me. I like being strong.”

branchLines.speaker: PLAYER
branchLines.text: “I wanted to make things easier.”

branchLines.speaker: KAEDRA
branchLines.text: “I asked for somewhere to rest. You are offering to take over my life.”

branchLines.speaker: NARRATOR
branchLines.text: Kaedra steps back and studies the offer like a badly fastened clasp. Then she declines it.

introLines.speaker: NARRATOR
introLines.text: Kaedra greets you without a bow. It is friendlier than a bow. It is also a question.

introLines.speaker: KAEDRA
introLines.text: “I have thought about your proposal. It matters too much to pretend we understood each other.”

introLines.speaker: PLAYER
introLines.text: “So have I.”

introLines.speaker: KAEDRA
introLines.text: “I do not want to be a legend you kneel to. Or to have a guardian appointed to protect me from myself.”

introLines.speaker: KAEDRA
introLines.text: “Can you see a life with the actual person standing here?”

options.labelText: “Yes. I made you a symbol, then a project. Wrong both times. I love the real you: capable, kind, sometimes tired, your own boss. Marry me?”

branchLines.speaker: KAEDRA
branchLines.text: “You have learned to make a short speech.”

branchLines.speaker: PLAYER
branchLines.text: “I can make it longer.”

branchLines.speaker: KAEDRA
branchLines.text: “Please do not.”

branchLines.speaker: NARRATOR
branchLines.text: She takes your hand. Her smile has none of the court in it.

branchLines.speaker: KAEDRA

branchLines.speaker: KAEDRA

branchLines.speaker: PLAYER
branchLines.text: “I guess I still don’t get it.”

branchLines.speaker: KAEDRA
branchLines.text: “Then I would rather wait than marry a misunderstanding.”

branchLines.speaker: NARRATOR

KAE-MID-01.title: The Royal Trial (first full midpoint attempt)

introLines.speaker: NARRATOR
introLines.text: The Palace Court is holding the Royal Trial, a ceremony to honor the kingdom’s guardians.

introLines.speaker: NARRATOR
introLines.text: Unofficially, it is testing how much bronze will fit on one podium.

introLines.speaker: KAEDRA
introLines.text: “Sixth speech. Thirty-one pages. All of them praising my ability to stand still.”

introLines.speaker: PLAYER
introLines.text: “Do they know you have other talents?”

introLines.speaker: KAEDRA
introLines.text: “One day I may demonstrate sitting.”

introLines.speaker: NARRATOR
introLines.text: A herald invites her to light a ceremonial warding sigil above the platform. It is meant to glow for a moment, symbolically.

introLines.speaker: HERALD
introLines.text: “A gentle flame, Your Highness! Just enough for the court to admire its protection!”

introLines.speaker: KAEDRA
introLines.text: “Understood. Keep the aisle clear.”

introLines.speaker: NARRATOR
introLines.text: She raises one hand. A thin band of amber light traces the sigil.

introLines.speaker: NARRATOR
introLines.text: Then a spark snaps sideways and pops against the empty edge of the platform.

introLines.speaker: NARRATOR
introLines.text: Nobody is struck. An attendant flinches. Half the front row tries to leave through the same door and trips over the other half.

introLines.speaker: NARRATOR
introLines.text: The spark fizzles out well short of the banners.

introLines.speaker: HERALD
introLines.text: “Remain calm! Move away from the platform in an orderly—my shoe! Has anyone seen my shoe?”

introLines.speaker: KAEDRA
introLines.text: “That was not the pattern I intended.”

introLines.speaker: NARRATOR
introLines.text: She closes her hand, and the sigil goes dark at once. Her wings stay folded. Her eyes are already on the crowded aisle.

introLines.speaker: PLAYER
introLines.text: “The spark’s out. People are bunching up at the doorway.”

introLines.speaker: KAEDRA
introLines.text: “Yes. They saw it. They saw me lose control.”

options.labelText: “Your magic’s stopped. Let’s give people room and have the attendants clear the aisle. Then talk somewhere quiet?”

branchLines.speaker: KAEDRA
branchLines.text: “Yes. Tell the herald the side aisle is clear. I will check the platform.”

branchLines.speaker: NARRATOR
branchLines.text: You steer people toward the side aisle while the attendants open the way. Kaedra checks the platform edge, then every face in the front row.

branchLines.speaker: NARRATOR
branchLines.text: Nobody is hurt. The room settles. Someone hands the herald back his shoe.

branchLines.speaker: HERALD
branchLines.text: “The ceremony has concluded! The speeches will resume after an interval of several years.”

branchLines.speaker: NARRATOR
branchLines.text: Later, under an arch within the Palace Court, Kaedra stands with her arms folded hard, holding herself steady.

branchLines.speaker: KAEDRA
branchLines.text: “When it went sideways, I knew how to stop it.”

branchLines.speaker: KAEDRA
branchLines.text: “I also knew what they would think. That I had finally become the danger they were waiting for.”

branchLines.speaker: PLAYER
branchLines.text: “You stopped it in a second, then counted the front row. I watched.”

branchLines.speaker: KAEDRA
branchLines.text: “They ask me to be a shield. Nobody has written the regulations for a shield that gets frightened.”

branchLines.speaker: KAEDRA
branchLines.text: “I thought you might come here to admire the spectacle.”

branchLines.speaker: KAEDRA
branchLines.text: “Or to tell me I need protecting from myself.”

branchLines.text: “I came for you, not the spectacle. What happens next is yours.”

branchLines.text: The line of her jaw loosens. She lets out a long, slow breath.

branchLines.text: “That is an unreasonably sensible answer. I may have to invite you to future ceremonies. As a precaution.”

branchLines.text: “Do they come with fewer speeches?”

branchLines.speaker: KAEDRA
branchLines.text: “I do not make promises I cannot keep.”

branchLines.speaker: KAEDRA
branchLines.text: “But stay a little longer?”

branchLines.text: “No.”

branchLines.speaker: KAEDRA
branchLines.text: “A frightened crowd is not an audience I need to impress.”

branchLines.speaker: PLAYER
branchLines.text: “I was trying to be supportive.”

branchLines.speaker: KAEDRA
branchLines.text: “I know. You meant the bigger one as a compliment.”

introLines.text: “People assume I am angry when I am silent.”

introLines.text: “Are you?”

branchLines.text: “Very well. A herald walks into a library. He is still talking.”

branchLines.speaker: KAEDRA
branchLines.text: “It worked better as a silence.”

introLines.text: “I am told that sitting is respectable when nothing is on fire.”

introLines.text: “Only if the building is made of exceptionally nervous paper.”

introLines.speaker: NARRATOR
introLines.text: Her nose twitches. The man with the papers breaks into a jog.

introLines.text: “Dust. I did not even sneeze.”

branchLines.speaker: KAEDRA

NER-EPI-01.title: Marriage epilogue: A Future She Chooses

introLines.speaker: NARRATOR
introLines.text: Moonwater Quay has never looked so dignified. Pearl ribbons hang over the water, and floating lanterns mark a clear channel for the ocean guests.

introLines.speaker: NARRATOR
introLines.text: The land guests line the stone railings, leaning over as far as manners allow.

introLines.speaker: NARRATOR
introLines.text: Someone has made a seating chart for a celebration where half the guests have no use for seats. It is on its ninth revision.

introLines.speaker: PLAYER
introLines.text: “I think the seating chart has declared war on geometry.”

introLines.speaker: NERELLE
introLines.text: “Three times I have told them. Currents are not assigned tables.”

introLines.speaker: NARRATOR
introLines.text: Nerelle waits in the water at the head of the channel.

introLines.speaker: NARRATOR
introLines.text: Her tail keeps time under the surface. Nobody has brought a spell.

introLines.speaker: NERELLE
introLines.text: “Before we begin, an announcement. I have arranged my duties with the council.”

introLines.speaker: NERELLE
introLines.text: “I will go on serving the ocean court. I will also go on making journeys, whenever I see fit.”

introLines.speaker: NARRATOR
introLines.text: A murmur runs through the sea guests. A stern court official consults a list, hesitates, then adds a new heading.

introLines.speaker: NARRATOR
introLines.text: *Arrangements Actually Discussed With the Princess.*

introLines.speaker: NERELLE
introLines.text: “Look at that. Reform is spreading.”

introLines.speaker: PLAYER
introLines.text: “Should I give a speech about our unprecedented cross-cultural scheduling achievements?”

introLines.speaker: NERELLE
introLines.text: “You prepared a speech?”

introLines.speaker: PLAYER
introLines.text: “Only twelve pages. I cut the appendix.”

introLines.speaker: NERELLE
introLines.text: “How merciful.”

introLines.speaker: NARRATOR
introLines.text: Then come the vows.

introLines.speaker: NERELLE
introLines.text: “I promise to ask before I decide for both of us. And to keep meeting you where the land runs into the sea.”

introLines.speaker: NERELLE
introLines.text: “I choose you, {PLAYER}. And my people. And my home. And every question I have not asked yet.”

introLines.speaker: PLAYER
introLines.text: “I’m yours, Nerelle. Keep telling me when I’m wrong about a current.”

introLines.speaker: NERELLE
introLines.text: “Then it’ll be a long marriage. You’re wrong about currents quite often.”

introLines.speaker: NARRATOR
introLines.text: Later, beside the Gardens canal, Nerelle drifts in the water while you sit on the bank with your feet in it beside her.

introLines.speaker: PLAYER
introLines.text: “Do you think we planned enough?”

introLines.speaker: NERELLE
introLines.text: “Enough to begin.”

introLines.speaker: NERELLE
introLines.text: “Also, your foot is in the wrong current. It’s about to visit the sea court without you.”

introLines.speaker: NARRATOR
introLines.text: Ribbons hang from the railings. On the water, small lanterns bob in rows, each painted with a name or a wish.

introLines.speaker: NARRATOR
introLines.text: Lit or unlit, they float. That appears to be the main requirement.

introLines.speaker: NERELLE
introLines.text: “Welcome to the Moonwater Festival. Officially, the lanterns honor those who guided us home.”

introLines.speaker: NERELLE
introLines.text: “Unofficially, everyone enjoys making things float, and then we call it solemn.”

introLines.speaker: PLAYER
introLines.text: “Both can be true.”

introLines.speaker: NERELLE
introLines.text: “Exactly. You’re getting good at this. It’s unsettling.”

introLines.speaker: NARRATOR
introLines.text: A cluster of young sea-dwellers steers a string of lanterns toward her. Nerelle greets every one of them by name.

introLines.speaker: NARRATOR
introLines.text: Then she listens to their concerns one at a time, including a long one about a crab.

introLines.speaker: PLAYER
introLines.text: “They’re glad you’re here.”

introLines.speaker: NERELLE
introLines.text: “This is my favorite part. They bring me real problems, and sometimes I can help.”

introLines.speaker: NERELLE
introLines.text: “The crab is a real problem. I have met him.”

introLines.speaker: PLAYER
introLines.text: “And the parts you don’t love?”

introLines.speaker: NERELLE
introLines.text: “Those exist too. I used to accept every demand, until there was no room left to want anything.”

introLines.speaker: NERELLE
introLines.text: “Now I am sorting them. Duties that are mine. Duties I can share. Habits dressed up as laws.”

introLines.speaker: NERELLE
introLines.text: “The third pile is the largest. The council is very attached to it.”

introLines.speaker: NARRATOR
introLines.text: A lantern drifts into an eddy and turns twice. Then it points itself upstream, apparently bound for a different festival.

introLines.speaker: NERELLE
introLines.text: “That one has more independence than half the council.”

introLines.speaker: PLAYER
introLines.text: “Does it get a say in where it goes?”

introLines.speaker: NERELLE
introLines.text: “Partly. Currents are real. How you travel with them is another matter.”

introLines.speaker: NERELLE
introLines.text: “I want to keep serving my people. I also want to keep learning about yours.”

introLines.speaker: NERELLE
introLines.text: “People hear one wish and assume it cancels the other.”

introLines.speaker: NARRATOR
introLines.text: She turns from the lanterns to you, waiting to find out what you heard.

options.labelText: “Keep your people and keep exploring. You sort the piles, and I’ll listen to how they come out.”

branchLines.speaker: NERELLE
branchLines.text: “Oh, thank goodness. I had a twelve-page petition prepared.”

branchLines.speaker: PLAYER
branchLines.text: “I can still fill out a form, if it helps.”

branchLines.speaker: NERELLE
branchLines.text: “Don’t tempt me. I know several excellent forms.”

branchLines.speaker: NARRATOR
branchLines.text: She reaches the wayward lantern with a flick of her tail and nudges it back into the channel with the others.

branchLines.speaker: NERELLE
branchLines.text: “The sea is my home. And there is a part of me I am still finding out about.”

branchLines.speaker: NERELLE
branchLines.text: “I would like anyone close to me to love the whole of that.”

branchLines.speaker: PLAYER
branchLines.text: “The whole of it. Crab included.”

branchLines.speaker: NERELLE
branchLines.text: “Especially the crab.”

options.labelText: “Couldn’t someone else do the ceremonies? Then you’d have all your time for exploring.”

branchLines.speaker: NERELLE
branchLines.text: “Some of them, yes. This one I would not give away.”

branchLines.speaker: PLAYER
branchLines.text: “I thought it’d make things easier.”

branchLines.speaker: NERELLE
branchLines.text: “It would. The way a boat is lighter with half of it missing.”

branchLines.speaker: NARRATOR
branchLines.text: A young sea-dweller calls her name. She turns to answer, and the conversation ends there.

options.labelText: “This all seems pointless. They’d manage fine without you.”

branchLines.speaker: NERELLE
branchLines.text: “You have been here for one lantern. I have been here for all of them.”

branchLines.speaker: PLAYER
branchLines.text: “I didn’t mean it like that.”

branchLines.speaker: NERELLE
branchLines.text: “You did. Now, if you will excuse me, I am going to be pointless with my people.”

branchLines.speaker: NARRATOR
branchLines.text: She swims out among the festival-goers. Nobody in the water asks you to follow.

introLines.speaker: NARRATOR
introLines.text: A row of small waterproof parcels bobs below the railing. Each is tied with a ribbon so precise that a court clerk would weep.

introLines.speaker: NERELLE
introLines.text: “Do you have a moment? I have been conducting an extremely unscientific study of surface souvenirs.”

introLines.speaker: PLAYER
introLines.text: “What did you find?”

introLines.speaker: NERELLE
introLines.text: “You sell seashells. To people living next to the sea.”

introLines.speaker: NERELLE
introLines.text: “They cost more if someone has written *Authentic Ocean* on them. I checked with the ocean. It denies writing that.”

introLines.speaker: PLAYER
introLines.text: “That’s advertising. Where I come from, it’s far more advanced.”

introLines.speaker: NERELLE
introLines.text: “More advanced? Could it convince a fish to buy water?”

introLines.speaker: PLAYER
introLines.text: “Give it a few fiscal quarters.”

introLines.speaker: NARRATOR
introLines.text: She laughs and nudges one parcel to the edge of the stone.

introLines.speaker: NARRATOR
introLines.text: Inside are a piece of sea glass and a folded sketch of a harbor lantern.

introLines.speaker: NERELLE
introLines.text: “A child in the tide villages gave me the glass. She said it looks like the surface lights when the water is calm.”

introLines.speaker: NERELLE
introLines.text: “The sketch is my attempt to see what she meant. The lantern came out looking like a worried turnip.”

introLines.speaker: PLAYER
introLines.text: “Did you ask her what she meant?”

introLines.speaker: NERELLE
introLines.text: “I tried. She recognized me halfway through and started answering as if she were being graded.”

introLines.speaker: NERELLE
introLines.text: “It is the crown. It turns ‘what do you mean?’ into an examination.”

introLines.speaker: NERELLE
introLines.text: “I would like to be curious about people without making them a royal research project.”

introLines.speaker: NERELLE
introLines.text: “My current theory involves fewer official seals.”

introLines.speaker: NARRATOR
introLines.text: She holds out the sketch for your opinion, and watches your face instead of the paper.

options.labelText: “Practice on me. Ask what I see in the lantern. I’ll answer badly, and you’re not allowed to grade it.”

branchLines.speaker: NERELLE
branchLines.text: “Ungraded. The council would faint.”

branchLines.speaker: NERELLE
branchLines.text: “Very well. What do you see?”

branchLines.speaker: PLAYER
branchLines.text: “A worried turnip.”

branchLines.speaker: NARRATOR
branchLines.text: She laughs, and turns to the real lantern’s reflection on the water.

branchLines.speaker: NARRATOR
branchLines.text: Her fin moves beneath it, and the reflection breaks into a dozen small lights.

branchLines.speaker: NERELLE
branchLines.text: “Oh. This is her sky.”

branchLines.speaker: NERELLE
branchLines.text: “She was telling me what home looks like from below.”

branchLines.speaker: PLAYER
branchLines.text: “Worth remembering.”

branchLines.speaker: NERELLE
branchLines.text: “I’ll remember it. I won’t, however, commission a commemorative plaque.”

options.labelText: “Oh, I can explain this. Souvenirs are symbolic. There’s a whole economy of sentimental objects.”

branchLines.speaker: NARRATOR
branchLines.text: You explain the whole economy of sentimental objects. It has four sections and a summary.

branchLines.speaker: NERELLE
branchLines.text: “Very thorough. I was asking about one girl and one lantern.”

branchLines.speaker: NERELLE
branchLines.text: “If I had wanted a lecture, I would have invited the royal tax assessor.”

branchLines.speaker: NARRATOR
branchLines.text: She tucks the sketch back into its parcel and reties the ribbon, just as precisely as before.

options.labelText: “How are you a princess and still need surface stuff explained?”

branchLines.speaker: NERELLE
branchLines.text: “I am a princess of the *sea*. I had assumed the tail made that clear.”

branchLines.speaker: NERELLE
branchLines.text: “There are nine currents within a mile of here. I can name all of them. Shall I explain them to you, slowly?”

branchLines.speaker: NARRATOR
branchLines.text: She closes the parcel herself. Her goodbye is polite, and very short.

NER-FIN-01.title: A Future She Chooses (first full final proposal)

introLines.speaker: NARRATOR
introLines.text: The conversation is over, and Nerelle has not swum away. She rests one hand on the waterside stone.

introLines.speaker: NERELLE
introLines.text: “You have become good company, for a surface traveler. I do not award that lightly.”

introLines.speaker: NERELLE
introLines.text: “My standards include knowing which end of a boat goes in the water.”

introLines.speaker: PLAYER
introLines.text: “Both ends, ideally.”

introLines.speaker: NERELLE
introLines.text: “You are improving.”

introLines.speaker: NARRATOR
introLines.text: She laughs. Then her fin settles against the current, the way it does when she means to stay.

introLines.speaker: NERELLE
introLines.text: “I need to say something before you say whatever you have been rehearsing.”

introLines.speaker: PLAYER
introLines.text: “What if I haven’t rehearsed anything?”

introLines.speaker: NERELLE
introLines.text: “Then this will be our most efficient conversation yet.”

introLines.speaker: NERELLE
introLines.text: “I have spoken with the people responsible for my duties. Some of the work, I will share.”

introLines.speaker: NERELLE
introLines.text: “The duties that are mine, I will keep. And I will go on exploring the surface waterways whenever I wish.”

introLines.speaker: PLAYER
introLines.text: “How did that go?”

introLines.speaker: NERELLE
introLines.text: “There were many documents. Three council members went noticeably grayer. I counted.”

introLines.speaker: NERELLE
introLines.text: “We will disagree, sometimes. Some days my people will need me. Some days I will need quiet.”

introLines.speaker: NERELLE
introLines.text: “None of that makes me want a life with you any less.”

introLines.speaker: NERELLE
introLines.text: “I will not leave the ocean to become someone’s idea of a proper bride.”

introLines.speaker: NERELLE
introLines.text: “And I will not ask you to give up your life and call it devotion.”

introLines.speaker: PLAYER
introLines.text: “Then what do you want?”

introLines.speaker: NERELLE
introLines.text: “A partnership. Honest plans. Places to meet where the water reaches the shore. Room to keep learning.”

introLines.speaker: NARRATOR
introLines.text: She reaches up from the water and offers her hand, the way one head of state offers it to another.

options.labelText: “I love your curiosity, your care for people, and that you know your own mind. Your future’s yours. Marry me, and we’ll build it together?”

branchLines.speaker: NERELLE
branchLines.text: “You really heard every word.”

branchLines.speaker: PLAYER
branchLines.text: “I tried. I’ll probably need reminders.”

branchLines.speaker: NERELLE
branchLines.text: “Good. I have already prepared several. They are in alphabetical order.”

branchLines.speaker: NARRATOR
branchLines.text: She looks out at the tide for a moment. It keeps moving. Then she turns back to you.

branchLines.speaker: NERELLE
branchLines.text: “Yes, {PLAYER}.”

branchLines.speaker: NERELLE
branchLines.text: “The ocean is still my home. My duties are still real. And there is room for us, if we keep making it.”

branchLines.speaker: PLAYER
branchLines.text: “I don’t know every part of what comes next.”

branchLines.speaker: NERELLE
branchLines.text: “Neither do I. I used to think that meant I had failed to plan.”

branchLines.speaker: PLAYER
branchLines.text: “And now?”

branchLines.speaker: NERELLE
branchLines.text: “Now I think it means we write a few pages together. In waterproof ink.”

branchLines.speaker: NARRATOR
branchLines.text: She takes your hand across the waterside stone. Hers is cold from the water, and does not let go.

introLines.speaker: NARRATOR
introLines.text: Nerelle is waiting in the water below the quay.

introLines.speaker: NARRATOR
introLines.text: A folded chart sits on a dry ledge within her reach, weighted down with a smooth stone.

introLines.speaker: NERELLE
introLines.text: “Before you ask: yes, this map is mine. No, I did not steal it.”

introLines.speaker: NERELLE
introLines.text: “The court has ruled that it is an inconvenient thing for me to own.”

introLines.speaker: PLAYER
introLines.text: “Is this the part where the warning says ‘forbidden journey’?”

introLines.speaker: NERELLE
introLines.text: “It says ‘unsanctioned surface observation.’ Written large enough, that sounds almost respectable.”

introLines.speaker: NARRATOR
introLines.text: She unfolds the chart. Spots near the quay and along the gardens canal are circled in neat ink.

introLines.speaker: NARRATOR
introLines.text: From each one, you could hear a market without leaving the water.

introLines.speaker: NARRATOR
introLines.text: One circle is labeled *bakery (smell only)*.

introLines.speaker: NERELLE
introLines.text: “I know these tides. I have guided emergency supplies through these channels.”

introLines.speaker: NERELLE
introLines.text: “But when I ask to come here because I want to, the answer changes.”

introLines.speaker: PLAYER
introLines.text: “Your court doesn’t want you to go?”

introLines.speaker: NERELLE
introLines.text: “They want me safe. They also want me available whenever a council member discovers another urgent meeting.”

introLines.speaker: NERELLE
introLines.text: “Both are reasonable. Added together, they come to every hour I have.”

introLines.speaker: NARRATOR
introLines.text: Overhead, a courier crosses a bridge under a stack of documents taller than his head. The top sheet escapes and drops toward the canal.

introLines.speaker: NARRATOR
introLines.text: Nerelle catches it before it sinks.

introLines.speaker: NERELLE
introLines.text: “Marked *urgent*. So the surface defends itself with paperwork too. I feel at home already.”

introLines.speaker: PLAYER
introLines.text: “Why tell me about this now?”

introLines.speaker: NERELLE
introLines.text: “Because I trust you. That makes it harder.”

introLines.speaker: NERELLE
introLines.text: “Everyone has an opinion about what I should do. I wanted to hear yours.”

introLines.speaker: NERELLE
introLines.text: “And I am afraid it will be one more order, dressed up as kindness.”

introLines.speaker: PLAYER
introLines.text: “What do you want?”

introLines.speaker: NERELLE
introLines.text: “To learn how people live above the water. To stay answerable to everyone below it who relies on me.”

introLines.speaker: NERELLE
introLines.text: “And for the choice to be mine.”

introLines.speaker: NARRATOR
introLines.text: She waits in the current with the chart between you. There is a pencil on top of it.

options.labelText: “Then let’s plan it. Your route, your timing. We find a safe stop, agree what to tell the court, and reschedule if the tide or council objects.”

branchLines.speaker: NERELLE
branchLines.text: “You did not start with what I am allowed to do.”

branchLines.speaker: PLAYER
branchLines.text: “Well, you know this water better than I ever will. I can do the surface bits, if you want them.”

branchLines.speaker: NERELLE
branchLines.text: “Then here is my proposal. First, I finish my scheduled hearings.”

branchLines.speaker: NERELLE
branchLines.text: “Second, I tell the appropriate attendants where I will be.”

branchLines.speaker: NERELLE
branchLines.text: “Third, I explore the garden canal. For no reason at all, except that I want to.”

branchLines.speaker: PLAYER
branchLines.text: “And if somebody calls a private outing scandalous?”

branchLines.speaker: NERELLE
branchLines.text: “I will ask whether they prefer their scandals alphabetized.”

branchLines.speaker: NARRATOR
branchLines.text: She traces the canal on the chart. You point out where a walkway runs along the bank.

branchLines.speaker: NERELLE
branchLines.text: “Not there. The current is too swift by that bridge. You would spend the visit waving at me as I went past.”

branchLines.speaker: NARRATOR
branchLines.text: She moves your finger two bridges down, to where the water slows.

branchLines.speaker: NERELLE
branchLines.text: “I was afraid you would turn this into a daring rescue.”

branchLines.speaker: NERELLE
branchLines.text: “Nobody needs to carry me away from my life. I would like room to live in it.”

branchLines.speaker: PLAYER
branchLines.text: “No daring rescue. I’ll cancel the horse.”

branchLines.speaker: NERELLE
branchLines.text: “You do not have a horse.”

branchLines.speaker: PLAYER
branchLines.text: “I was going to borrow one.”

branchLines.speaker: NARRATOR
branchLines.text: You follow the canal together, you on the path and she in the water beside you.

branchLines.speaker: NARRATOR
branchLines.text: She points out which bridges echo, and which only pretend to.

introLines.speaker: NARRATOR
introLines.text: An official-looking sheet drifts by. Nerelle fishes it out and reads it, dripping.

introLines.speaker: NERELLE
introLines.text: “A surface office has issued a permit for pleasant weather. It has a seal.”

introLines.speaker: PLAYER
introLines.text: “Does the sea council do anything like that?”

introLines.speaker: NERELLE
introLines.text: “We issue warnings, not commands to clouds. It saves embarrassment.”

introLines.speaker: NARRATOR
introLines.text: A single fat raindrop lands on the seal.

introLines.speaker: NERELLE
introLines.text: “The clouds have replied.”

options.labelText: “Want to stamp it ‘Declined by the clouds’ and send it back?”

branchLines.speaker: NERELLE
branchLines.text: “Yes. I carry waterproof ink for exactly this.”

branchLines.speaker: NARRATOR
branchLines.text: She writes *Declined by the clouds* across the seal, in a hand much neater than the office’s.

options.labelText: “Your council should try one. A permit for one nice day can’t hurt.”

branchLines.speaker: NERELLE
branchLines.text: “And when the permitted day rains, whom do they blame?”

branchLines.speaker: NERELLE
branchLines.text: “I have no wish to become personally responsible for thunder.”

introLines.speaker: NARRATOR
introLines.text: The tide has turned. Every rope tied along the edge hangs at a new angle.

introLines.speaker: NERELLE
introLines.text: “Everything has moved since we last spoke. The eddy by the wall is gone. There is a new one by your foot.”

introLines.speaker: PLAYER
introLines.text: “Doesn’t that get tiring?”

introLines.speaker: NERELLE
introLines.text: “It means I get a new place twice a day without the trouble of moving house.”

introLines.speaker: NERELLE
introLines.text: “Surface people move once a decade and complain about it for a year.”

options.labelText: “Honestly, where’s the good current now? Quiz me.”

branchLines.speaker: NERELLE
branchLines.text: “Very well. Point to where you would swim.”

branchLines.speaker: NARRATOR
branchLines.text: You point at the calmest patch of water. She points, with great patience, at the patch beside it.

branchLines.speaker: NERELLE
branchLines.text: “Close. Yours would have taken you very politely out to sea.”

options.labelText: “You could pick one route and stick to it. Less to keep track of.”

branchLines.speaker: NERELLE
branchLines.text: “I could. For about six hours.”

branchLines.speaker: NERELLE
branchLines.text: “Then the tide turns, and my route goes straight into the wall.”

introLines.speaker: NERELLE
introLines.text: “A merchant just told his friend that their meeting went swimmingly.”

introLines.speaker: NERELLE
introLines.text: “Was the meeting held in a current? Were there eels?”

introLines.speaker: PLAYER
introLines.text: “It means it went well.”

introLines.speaker: NERELLE
introLines.text: “Well? Half of swimming is not drowning. The other half is eels.”

introLines.speaker: NARRATOR
introLines.text: Up on the walkway, the merchant is still telling people how swimmingly it went.

options.labelText: “So we took your hardest skill and made it mean ‘fine’?”

branchLines.speaker: NERELLE
branchLines.text: “Without asking. I am drafting a complaint.”

branchLines.speaker: NERELLE
branchLines.text: “Polite. Firm. Waterproof.”

options.labelText: “To be fair, swimming must be pretty easy for you.”

branchLines.speaker: NERELLE
branchLines.text: “Easy the way stairs are easy for you.”

branchLines.speaker: NERELLE
branchLines.text: “Ask me again in a riptide.”

introLines.speaker: NARRATOR
introLines.text: A leaf is turning slow circles beside Nerelle. It shows no sign of leaving.

introLines.speaker: NERELLE
introLines.text: “It has been waiting there for several minutes. I suspect an appointment.”

introLines.speaker: PLAYER
introLines.text: “Does it need your signature?”

introLines.speaker: NERELLE
introLines.text: “I don’t recall issuing permits to leaves.”

introLines.speaker: NARRATOR
introLines.text: A second leaf drifts up and settles in behind the first. Then a third.

introLines.speaker: NERELLE
introLines.text: “Oh no. It’s a queue.”

options.labelText: “Put up a sign: *Back after the tide.* You’re off duty.”

branchLines.speaker: NERELLE
branchLines.text: “Back after the tide. The council would never.”

branchLines.speaker: NARRATOR
branchLines.text: She tells the leaves. They drift off politely, one at a time, in order.

options.labelText: “Keep the first one! Press it and frame it. First official leaf of your reign.”

branchLines.speaker: NERELLE
branchLines.text: “Then the other two will want frames.”

branchLines.speaker: NARRATOR
branchLines.text: The queue grows by a twig.

introLines.text: Nerelle reties the knot on a floating marker without looking at her hands.

introLines.speaker: NERELLE
introLines.text: “A sailor taught me this knot. He insisted his grandmother invented it.”

introLines.speaker: PLAYER
introLines.text: “Did she?”

introLines.speaker: NERELLE
introLines.text: “Possibly. Six other grandmothers have made the same claim.”

introLines.speaker: NERELLE
introLines.text: “Two have written to the council. One enclosed a diagram and a threat.”

options.labelText: “Call it the grandmothers’ knot. All seven of them.”

branchLines.speaker: NERELLE
branchLines.text: “Seven signatories. That is more than our last trade agreement.”

branchLines.speaker: NERELLE
branchLines.text: “I will propose it. Through a very junior clerk, in case of diagrams.”

options.labelText: “Let’s settle it. Someone must have written down who tied it first.”

branchLines.speaker: NERELLE
branchLines.text: “You would take on seven grandmothers?”

branchLines.speaker: NERELLE
branchLines.text: “Brave. I’ll tie something nice for your memorial.”

introLines.speaker: NARRATOR
introLines.text: A floating marker keeps bumping the waterside stone. Nerelle is counting the bumps.

introLines.speaker: NERELLE
introLines.text: “Your clock tower claims every hour is the same length. I have been checking.”

introLines.speaker: PLAYER
introLines.text: “How’s the claim holding up?”

introLines.speaker: NERELLE
introLines.text: “Poorly. The tide has filed a dissent.”

introLines.speaker: NERELLE
introLines.text: “At home, we ask the moon what time it is. In emergencies, a very old crab.”

options.labelText: “Keep the crab. The tower can have the meetings.”

branchLines.speaker: NERELLE
branchLines.text: “Agreed. I’ll inform the crab.”

branchLines.speaker: NERELLE
branchLines.text: “He has been anxious about his position.”

options.labelText: “We could merge them. One clock, with the tides as a recurring event.”

branchLines.speaker: NERELLE
branchLines.text: “Splendid. Please inform the moon before the council.”

branchLines.speaker: NARRATOR
branchLines.text: The marker bumps the stone again. By the tower’s reckoning, the tide is four minutes behind.

introLines.speaker: NARRATOR
introLines.text: A bell rings somewhere above the water. Nerelle ducks under to listen, then surfaces.

introLines.speaker: NERELLE
introLines.text: “Underwater, that bell is lower and lasts longer. It sounds as if it means it.”

introLines.speaker: PLAYER
introLines.text: “What else can you hear down there?”

introLines.speaker: NERELLE
introLines.text: “Mostly boats. Their owners assume that if I am underwater, I cannot complain.”

introLines.speaker: NERELLE
introLines.text: “I can. There is a barge with a squeaking rudder that I have written to three times.”

options.labelText: “What does the squeaky barge sound like from down there?”

branchLines.speaker: NERELLE
branchLines.text: “Like a gull being disappointed very slowly.”

branchLines.speaker: NERELLE
branchLines.text: “Put your ear to the water when it passes. I will provide commentary.”

options.labelText: “Couldn’t you swim further out, away from the noise?”

branchLines.speaker: NERELLE
branchLines.text: “I could. Then the barge would win.”

branchLines.speaker: NARRATOR
branchLines.text: She does not move a fin’s width. Somewhere upstream, a rudder squeaks, and her eyes narrow.

options.labelText: “Maybe they’d listen if you weren’t so strange.”

branchLines.speaker: NERELLE
branchLines.text: “I can hear you perfectly. That is the problem.”

branchLines.speaker: NARRATOR
branchLines.text: She sinks out of sight. She hears the next bell without you.

introLines.speaker: NARRATOR
introLines.text: Two visitors have stopped on the path to greet Nerelle in the water. One bows. The other waves.

introLines.speaker: NARRATOR
introLines.text: Each notices the other and adds the missing gesture. Now both are bowing and waving at once.

introLines.speaker: NERELLE
introLines.text: “Etiquette has reached an impasse. The gestures are becoming competitive.”

introLines.speaker: PLAYER
introLines.text: “Is there an official rule?”

introLines.speaker: NERELLE
introLines.text: “Three ceremonial committees have studied the question. Their report is in its fourth volume.”

introLines.speaker: NARRATOR
introLines.text: The taller visitor adds a curtsy. A passing duck receives most of it.

options.labelText: “What do you like? A hello? A wave?”

branchLines.speaker: NERELLE
branchLines.text: “Three committees, and nobody thought to ask me.”

branchLines.speaker: NERELLE
branchLines.text: “Hello is perfect. A wave is lovely. Bowing to ducks is discouraged.”

options.labelText: “Bow, obviously. You can’t go wrong bowing to royalty.”

branchLines.speaker: NARRATOR
branchLines.text: The visitors overhear and bow low. Sea protocol says a bow must be returned, so Nerelle bows back. They bow again.

branchLines.speaker: NERELLE
branchLines.text: “This is how the last treaty signing took nine days.”

introLines.speaker: NARRATOR
introLines.text: A gull lands beside Nerelle, pulls a ribbon off a post, and drops it in the water in front of her.

introLines.speaker: NERELLE
introLines.text: “That is the gulls’ fourth petition this week.”

introLines.speaker: PLAYER
introLines.text: “What are they petitioning for?”

introLines.speaker: NERELLE
introLines.text: “Better decorations, they claim. Their actual demand is unattended crumbs.”

introLines.speaker: NERELLE
introLines.text: “I rejected the first three. They ate the third.”

introLines.speaker: NARRATOR
introLines.text: The gull is now staring at your pocket.

options.labelText: “Petition denied. My pocket stays shut.”

branchLines.speaker: NERELLE
branchLines.text: “A united front. The fish thank you.”

branchLines.speaker: NARRATOR
branchLines.text: The gull looks at your pocket, then at your face, and appears to memorize it.

options.labelText: “Aw, one crumb won’t hurt. It’s only one gull.”

branchLines.speaker: NARRATOR
branchLines.text: You toss one crumb. Nine more gulls arrive.

branchLines.speaker: NERELLE
branchLines.text: “Congratulations. You have formally recognized their government.”

introLines.speaker: NARRATOR
introLines.text: Nerelle draws a long curve on the wet stone with one finger, then adds three short ticks.

introLines.speaker: NERELLE
introLines.text: “Current strength, in court notation. What did your world use?”

introLines.speaker: PLAYER
introLines.text: “Graphs. And arguments about the graphs.”

introLines.speaker: NERELLE
introLines.text: “Ah. The argument. The one scientific instrument found in every civilization.”

introLines.speaker: NERELLE
introLines.text: “Three ticks means strong. *In a mood* has its own mark.”

options.labelText: “What’s the mark for ‘in a mood’?”

branchLines.speaker: NARRATOR
branchLines.text: She draws a tight, irritable little spiral.

branchLines.speaker: NERELLE
branchLines.text: “That one. We also use it for the treasury minister.”

options.labelText: “I could turn these into a proper graph for you. Axes, labels, the works.”

branchLines.speaker: NERELLE
branchLines.text: “How generous. Which axis is the mood on?”

branchLines.speaker: NARRATOR
branchLines.text: You do not have an axis for the mood. While you think about it, the curve dries off the stone.

introLines.speaker: NARRATOR
introLines.text: The towers above the water hang upside down in it, wobbling slightly.

introLines.speaker: NERELLE
introLines.text: “From down here, your city appears to be built underneath mine. Everyone is walking on the ceiling.”

introLines.speaker: PLAYER
introLines.text: “Does it look strange?”

introLines.speaker: NERELLE
introLines.text: “It looks very well run. Nobody in that one has ever asked me to sign anything.”

introLines.speaker: NARRATOR
introLines.text: A ripple passes through. The towers shiver apart and slowly reassemble.

introLines.speaker: NERELLE
introLines.text: “Ah. Renovations.”

options.labelText: “Hold on. Let me look from your height.”

branchLines.speaker: NARRATOR
branchLines.text: You kneel at the edge until your chin is nearly touching the water. The upside-down towers sway in front of you.

branchLines.speaker: NERELLE
branchLines.text: “Welcome. From here, you’re taller than the palace.”

options.labelText: “Technically the real city’s up here. That’s just light bouncing.”

branchLines.speaker: NERELLE
branchLines.text: “Thank you. We have light under the sea as well. It is how we see boats coming.”

branchLines.speaker: NERELLE
branchLines.text: “I preferred the upside-down city. It never explains things.”

introLines.speaker: NARRATOR
introLines.text: The Palace Court is dressed for a wedding. Nearly every dish wears a little label in the bride’s capitals: *SAFE*.

introLines.speaker: NARRATOR
introLines.text: The bride herself is inspecting her bouquet, stem by stem.

introLines.speaker: SENNA
introLines.text: “Lily of the valley. Beautiful. Nobody let the palace cat near it.”

introLines.speaker: PLAYER
introLines.text: “Is the palace cat invited?”

introLines.speaker: SENNA
introLines.text: “The palace cat attends everything. It has never once been invited.”

introLines.speaker: NARRATOR
introLines.text: Doctor Dorrance rises to give a toast. His cup of tea has been checked.

introLines.speaker: PHYSICIAN
introLines.text: “When Her Highness arrived with four trunks of what I took to be weeds, I gave her a week.”

introLines.speaker: PHYSICIAN
introLines.text: “She has since corrected my herbal in forty-three places. In pencil. I have kept every…”

introLines.speaker: NARRATOR
introLines.text: He doesn’t finish. He sits down and cries into a napkin, and then into Pim’s sleeve.

introLines.speaker: SENNA
introLines.text: “He kept them. That’s why he stopped putting leeches on burnt thumbs.”

introLines.speaker: NARRATOR
introLines.text: Then come the vows. Senna’s are numbered. You have never been so proud of anyone in your life.

introLines.speaker: SENNA
introLines.text: “One. I’ll check your tea. Two. I’ll tell you when you’re wrong about plants. That’ll be often.”

introLines.speaker: SENNA
introLines.text: “Three. I’ll always tell you when you’re about to eat something you shouldn’t.”

introLines.speaker: SENNA
introLines.text: “Don’t eat that.”

introLines.speaker: NARRATOR
introLines.text: You put down the canapé. It has a sprig of holly on top. Its label says *NOT FOOD*.

introLines.speaker: SENNA
introLines.text: “Four. There were nine. I cut five for being sentimental. One of them rhymed.”

introLines.speaker: NARRATOR
introLines.text: Later, in the Royal Gardens, Senna kneels at the physic beds in her wedding dress, with her gardening gloves on over the sleeves.

introLines.speaker: NARRATOR
introLines.text: Beside the label with both your names on it, one small green leaf has come up through the soil.

introLines.speaker: SENNA
introLines.text: “That’s early. The literature says four months. It’s been six weeks.”

introLines.speaker: PLAYER
introLines.text: “Maybe it likes us.”

introLines.speaker: SENNA
introLines.text: “Don’t be sentimental about a hellebore. It’s poisonous from root to petal.”

introLines.speaker: SENNA
introLines.text: “I don’t need anything. I want you here. That’s different. I checked.”

introLines.speaker: NARRATOR
introLines.text: She leans over and rests her forehead against yours. Then she goes back to watching the leaf.

introLines.speaker: SENNA
introLines.text: “Vow three. Don’t eat it.”

introLines.speaker: NARRATOR
introLines.text: Senna is standing with both hands in her apron pockets. Every pocket is empty.

introLines.speaker: SENNA
introLines.text: “I’ve been given a day off. By force.”

introLines.speaker: PLAYER
introLines.text: “Who forced you?”

introLines.speaker: SENNA
introLines.text: “Pim took my twine. Dorrance took my notebook. He’s reading it right now. I can feel it.”

introLines.speaker: NARRATOR
introLines.text: Pim skids up beside you, out of breath.

introLines.speaker: PIM
introLines.text: “Miss Senna! Doctor Dorrance says if you come back early, he’ll treat everyone himself! He’s got the leech jar out!”

introLines.speaker: SENNA
introLines.text: “He would, too. He’s been waiting years for this.”

introLines.speaker: NARRATOR
introLines.text: Pim runs off again, holding her bag of boiled sweets over his head like a trophy.

introLines.speaker: SENNA
introLines.text: “Nobody has so much as a splinter. I asked around.”

introLines.speaker: SENNA
introLines.text: “What do people do with a day that has nothing wrong in it?”

introLines.speaker: PLAYER
introLines.text: “So what do you like? Not for work. Just because.”

introLines.speaker: SENNA
introLines.text: “Mushrooms. Finding where they’ve come up. Looking at them without picking any.”

introLines.speaker: SENNA
introLines.text: “Pastries, too. But I can’t eat one without inspecting it, so that’s work again.”

introLines.speaker: NARRATOR
introLines.text: She takes her hands out of her empty pockets, then can’t seem to decide where to put them.

options.labelText: “Why not sort the jars? No patients, nobody rushing you. Just you and the labels.”

branchLines.speaker: SENNA
branchLines.text: “The jars. I’ve been meaning to redo the jars for weeks.”

branchLines.speaker: NARRATOR
branchLines.text: She spends her day off sorting them by name, then by how ill each could make you, then by name again.

branchLines.speaker: PIM
branchLines.text: “Miss Senna! You’re not supposed to be here!”

branchLines.speaker: SENNA
branchLines.text: “I’m not working. I’m resting. Alphabetically.”

branchLines.speaker: NARRATOR
branchLines.text: She seems happy. She also looks exactly the way she does every other day.

options.labelText: “Mushroom walk. Slow, no picking. Then pastries, and I’ll do the inspecting.”

branchLines.speaker: SENNA
branchLines.text: “A walk. With no patient at the end of it.”

branchLines.speaker: NARRATOR
branchLines.text: You walk slowly and look down a lot. Mushrooms turn out to be everywhere, once someone points.

branchLines.speaker: NARRATOR
branchLines.text: She keeps her gloved hands clasped behind her back, so they can’t pick anything.

branchLines.speaker: SENNA
branchLines.text: “*Amanita.* Gorgeous. Don’t touch it. Don’t even breathe on it rudely.”

branchLines.speaker: SENNA
branchLines.text: “That’s a puffball. A raindrop hits it and it sighs out a tiny cloud. Completely harmless. Shameless show-off.”

branchLines.speaker: NARRATOR
branchLines.text: Afterward you buy two pastries. You hand her one and tell her you’ve already inspected it. Personally.

branchLines.speaker: SENNA
branchLines.text: “Personally.”

branchLines.speaker: NARRATOR
branchLines.text: She inspects it again anyway. You let her. She hums through most of it.

branchLines.speaker: SENNA
branchLines.text: “Nothing went wrong all day. I kept checking.”

branchLines.speaker: SENNA
branchLines.text: “Same again next time they confiscate my pockets.”

options.labelText: “So you’re no fun unless someone’s ill. Good to know.”

branchLines.speaker: SENNA
branchLines.text: “Someone’s always ill. I’ll go and find them.”

branchLines.speaker: NARRATOR
branchLines.text: She leaves to find someone with a splinter. It doesn’t take her long.

introLines.speaker: NARRATOR
introLines.text: Pim skids up, waving a paper packet. On the front, a beaming old woman in a nightcap promises sleep.

introLines.speaker: PIM
introLines.text: “Senna! Gran bought this! *Grandmother’s Sleep Tea!* It’s got grandmother on it, so it’s safe, isn’t it? Can I have some?”

introLines.speaker: NARRATOR
introLines.text: Senna takes the packet and tweezes one gray-green leaf out of it. Then she goes very still.

introLines.speaker: SENNA
introLines.text: “Pim. Where did your gran buy this?”

introLines.speaker: PIM
introLines.text: “The market! There’s a queue! The man says it’s outselling honey!”

introLines.speaker: NARRATOR
introLines.text: Senna takes your sleeve and tows you, without explanation, to a market stall in the Town Square.

introLines.speaker: NARRATOR
introLines.text: A queue of yawning customers leads up to the stall. The merchant is scooping tea from a big jar labeled *GRANDMOTHER’S SLEEP TEA*.

introLines.speaker: MERCHANT
introLines.text: “One at a time, plenty for everyone! Princess! A big bag for you?”

introLines.speaker: SENNA
introLines.text: “No. Stop selling it.”

introLines.speaker: MERCHANT
introLines.text: “Stop? It’s my own grandmother’s recipe! Chamomile, lime flower, mullein. She drank it for ninety years!”

introLines.speaker: SENNA
introLines.text: “The chamomile’s fine. The lime flower’s fine. This isn’t mullein.”

introLines.speaker: SENNA
introLines.text: “*Digitalis purpurea*. Foxglove. Before it flowers, the leaves pass for mullein, if you’re in a hurry and you squint. Somebody squinted.”

introLines.speaker: SENNA
introLines.text: “In a teapot, it makes the heart trip over its own feet.”

introLines.speaker: MERCHANT
introLines.text: “Foxglove? I buy from a proper supplier! He has a cart! With his name painted on it!”

introLines.speaker: PLAYER
introLines.text: “A cart with his name on it. That’s basically a certification.”

introLines.speaker: MERCHANT
introLines.text: “With respect, Princess, you’ve looked at one leaf. One! I’ve got a living to make.”

introLines.speaker: NARRATOR
introLines.text: Senna looks at you. Both her hands are full of evidence, and the queue is still moving.

options.labelText: “Let’s report it to the guard tomorrow. No need to make a scene in front of everyone.”

branchLines.speaker: SENNA
branchLines.text: “Tomorrow.”

branchLines.speaker: NARRATOR
branchLines.text: At the front of the queue, a woman buys two bags. One’s for her mother.

branchLines.speaker: NARRATOR
branchLines.text: Senna climbs onto a crate and explains foxglove to the entire queue, loudly. The merchant hides behind his jar.

branchLines.speaker: SENNA
branchLines.text: “There. A scene.”

options.labelText: “Let’s check it against your herbal, right here. Can the sale wait five minutes while we look?”

branchLines.speaker: PLAYER
branchLines.text: “If she’s wrong, I’ll buy the first ten bags myself.”

branchLines.speaker: NARRATOR
branchLines.text: You slide her herbal out from under her arm and find *Digitalis*. You hold the leaf against the drawing while she points.

branchLines.speaker: SENNA
branchLines.text: “Turn it over. The veins make a net, and the edge has little teeth. Mullein’s smooth at the edge and woolly as a sock.”

branchLines.speaker: NARRATOR
branchLines.text: The merchant looks at the drawing, then at the leaf. His face goes the color of weak tea.

branchLines.speaker: PLAYER
branchLines.text: “Your supplier swapped the leaf. Anyone could’ve missed it.”

branchLines.speaker: SENNA
branchLines.text: “I didn’t.”

branchLines.speaker: MERCHANT
branchLines.text: “Anyone could’ve! Right! Sleep Tea’s off, everyone! Refunds at the front, and a free honey cake each!”

branchLines.speaker: SENNA
branchLines.text: “Nobody eat the honey cake until I’ve looked at it.”

branchLines.speaker: NARRATOR
branchLines.text: She relabels the jar *EVIDENCE*. Then she inspects a honey cake. It passes, and Pim gets the first one.

options.labelText: “Senna, come on. You think everything’s poison.”

branchLines.speaker: SENNA
branchLines.text: “I think this is foxglove. I think you’re standing in front of the queue.”

branchLines.speaker: NARRATOR
branchLines.text: She steps around you and opens her herbal for the merchant. She doesn’t show it to you.

meta.Type: optional Senna event, pre-midpoint, one-time.
meta.Eligibility: Current Senna route; intelligence ≥ 3; correct stage; Senna's scheduled slot; unused daily encounter.
