meta.Objective: The right answer gets the tea off sale with care and evidence while the merchant saves face, treating Senna’s expertise as real.
meta.END: Mark SEN-EVT-PRE-01 experienced regardless of result; commit the one net heart result.

introLines.speaker: NARRATOR
introLines.text: Senna takes you to the physic beds and hands you a trowel, handle first.

introLines.speaker: SENNA
introLines.text: “Kneel there. Mind the comfrey. Don’t eat the comfrey.”

introLines.speaker: NARRATOR
introLines.text: She kneels beside you with her gloves on and digs a hole exactly one knuckle deep. She checks it with the knuckle.

introLines.speaker: SENNA
introLines.text: “The packet I kept for myself. It turned out to be relevant.”

introLines.speaker: NARRATOR
introLines.text: She drops in one seed and pats the soil over it. Then she takes a small wooden label from her apron, already written in her square capitals.

introLines.speaker: NARRATOR
introLines.text: *HELLEBORUS NIGER. PLANTED BY: S. AND ________*

introLines.speaker: SENNA
introLines.text: “*Helleborus niger.* Poisonous from root to petal. It flowers in the snow, when nothing else can be bothered.”

introLines.speaker: SENNA
introLines.text: “You were going to find out in three years. I moved it up.”

introLines.speaker: PLAYER
introLines.text: “S. and…?”

introLines.speaker: SENNA
introLines.text: “I left a space. I measured it. One name wide.”

introLines.speaker: SENNA
introLines.text: “I don’t know what goes in it. I’ve rubbed it out twice.”

introLines.speaker: SENNA
introLines.text: “Pulse, fast. Hands, unreliable. Face, warm. I’d blame the sun, but there isn’t any.”

introLines.speaker: NARRATOR
introLines.text: She holds out the pencil from her bun. The sprig of rosemary comes with it and drops onto the soil.

introLines.speaker: SENNA
introLines.text: “Rosemary. For remembrance. That wasn’t on purpose.”

introLines.speaker: SENNA
introLines.text: “My mother sent me here to find someone who’d put up with me.”

introLines.speaker: SENNA
introLines.text: “So. What do I write?”

options.labelText: “Senna, ever since you swatted a tart out of my hand, I’ve known. You’re the rarest thing in this garden. Marry me?”

branchLines.speaker: SENNA
branchLines.text: “That was a speech. I asked you a question.”

branchLines.speaker: SENNA
branchLines.text: “You rehearsed it. You did a hand gesture on *rarest*.”

branchLines.speaker: PLAYER
branchLines.text: “It sounded better in my head.”

branchLines.speaker: NARRATOR
branchLines.text: She slides the label back into her apron. The space on it stays blank.

options.internalLabel: Wrong; no new heart penalty; marriage retry pending at ten hearts

options.labelText: “Marry me, and you’ll never have to work in an infirmary again. I’ll look after you for a change.”

branchLines.speaker: SENNA
branchLines.text: “…Why would I want that?”

branchLines.speaker: PLAYER
branchLines.text: “So you could rest. You never stop.”

branchLines.speaker: SENNA
branchLines.text: “I like the infirmary. I moved in with four trunks. Nobody made me.”

branchLines.speaker: NARRATOR
branchLines.text: She puts the label away in the pocket marked *sweets, for patients*. Then she goes back to weeding.

options.internalLabel: Wrong; no new heart penalty; marriage retry pending at ten hearts

options.labelText: “Write my name. Marry me. I want to be here when it flowers, and every year after.”

branchLines.speaker: NARRATOR
branchLines.text: Senna looks at the label. Then at you, for longer.

branchLines.speaker: SENNA
branchLines.text: “Your name.”

branchLines.speaker: PLAYER
branchLines.text: “Spelled right, ideally.”

branchLines.speaker: NARRATOR
branchLines.text: She writes your name in the space and gets a letter wrong. She rubs it out with her thumb and tries again.

branchLines.speaker: SENNA
branchLines.text: “Don’t watch. My hands have stopped taking instructions.”

branchLines.speaker: NARRATOR
branchLines.text: The second try is perfect. She pushes the label into the soil beside the seed, then straightens it. Twice.

branchLines.speaker: SENNA
branchLines.text: “Yes, {PLAYER}. Obviously.”

branchLines.speaker: SENNA
branchLines.text: “I’ve been diagnosing this for weeks.”

branchLines.speaker: PLAYER
branchLines.text: “What’s the diagnosis?”

branchLines.speaker: SENNA
branchLines.text: “Chronic. I looked for a cure. Then I stopped looking.”

branchLines.speaker: NARRATOR
branchLines.text: She takes your hand. Her glove leaves soil on your fingers, and she doesn’t apologize for it.

branchLines.speaker: SENNA
branchLines.text: “I’ll write to my mother. One line. *Found someone. Stop underlining.*”

options.internalLabel: Correct; terminal success and gallery unlock

meta.Type: mandatory first marriage proposal; full scene shown only once.
meta.Location: Opens where Senna is scheduled; presented at the Royal Gardens within the same encounter (not a new map location).
meta.Objective: Answer the label’s question plainly: write your name and ask to be there when it flowers, as a partner rather than a performer or a rescuer.
meta.END: Shares the originating action. Correct: terminal success and gallery unlock. Wrong: retry pending at ten hearts.

introLines.speaker: NARRATOR
introLines.text: Senna has the wooden label out before you reach her. Its corners have gone round from living in her apron.

introLines.speaker: SENNA
introLines.text: “The seed hasn’t come up. It’s a three-year seed. I check it anyway.”

introLines.speaker: NARRATOR
introLines.text: She holds out the label and the pencil from her bun.

introLines.speaker: SENNA
introLines.text: “Try again. Plainly.”

introLines.speaker: SENNA
introLines.text: “It has to fit on the label.”

options.labelText: “My name goes in the space. Marry me, and we’ll both be there when it flowers.”

branchLines.speaker: SENNA
branchLines.text: “That fits.”

branchLines.speaker: NARRATOR
branchLines.text: She writes your name in the space, spelled right on the first try. She checks it twice anyway.

branchLines.speaker: SENNA
branchLines.text: “Yes. Obviously. You only had to say it at label size.”

branchLines.speaker: NARRATOR
branchLines.text: She tucks the label into the apron pocket nearest her heart. She has measured which one that is.

options.internalLabel: Correct; terminal success, gallery unlock, no hearts gained

options.labelText: “Marry me once the infirmary can spare you. I don’t mind waiting until things calm down.”

branchLines.speaker: SENNA
branchLines.text: “When the infirmary can spare me.”

branchLines.speaker: SENNA
branchLines.text: “It won’t. Someone sprains something every day. I keep a chart.”

branchLines.speaker: NARRATOR
branchLines.text: The label goes back in her apron. On the way, she checks the space, in case your name has turned up by itself.

options.internalLabel: Wrong; keep ten hearts, retry pending

meta.Type: mandatory brief final retry; repeatable following a wrong final answer.
meta.Location: Senna's scheduled location.
meta.Objective: Fill in the label plainly: your name and a shared future, with no conditions and no speech.
meta.END: Every attempt consumes one slot and the daily encounter and creates one journal entry.

introLines.speaker: NARRATOR
introLines.text: Senna meets you with a lamp in one hand and a basket of herb bundles in the other. She gives you both.

introLines.speaker: SENNA
introLines.text: “Infirmary. The last patient’s gone home, so you can carry.”

introLines.speaker: NARRATOR
introLines.text: The infirmary is a narrow wing off the Palace Court. It smells of rosemary and clean linen, with a third smell you decide not to ask about.

introLines.speaker: NARRATOR
introLines.text: Pim is asleep on a cot by the stove, still holding half a rolled bandage.

introLines.speaker: SENNA
introLines.text: “He rolled forty bandages, then himself. I’m counting him as forty-one.”

introLines.speaker: NARRATOR
introLines.text: She sits at the long worktable and pulls the lamp close. A row of empty jars is waiting for labels.

introLines.speaker: SENNA
introLines.text: “Hold the twine. Tighter. It’s twine, not a sparrow.”

introLines.speaker: NARRATOR
introLines.text: She sorts dried leaves into the jars by smell. One pale root gets held up to the lamp and frowned at.

introLines.speaker: SENNA
introLines.text: “*Aconitum napellus.* Monkshood. The root looks like horseradish. Every so often a cook grates it over the beef, and the whole table’s mouth goes numb.”

introLines.speaker: SENNA
introLines.text: “I took a basket of it out of the palace kitchens. The cook thanked me, then asked me never to come back.”

introLines.speaker: NARRATOR
introLines.text: She labels the jar in square capitals: MONKSHOOD. NOT HORSERADISH. DO NOT GRATE. DO NOT, PIM.

introLines.speaker: PLAYER
introLines.text: “Does Pim try to eat the stock?”

introLines.speaker: SENNA
introLines.text: “Once. Lavender soap. In his defense, it was shaped like a cake.”

introLines.speaker: NARRATOR
introLines.text: From under her notebook she slides out a letter. It’s been folded and unfolded so often the paper has gone soft.

introLines.speaker: SENNA
introLines.text: “My mother. Hollowmere post. It always arrives damp.”

introLines.speaker: SENNA
introLines.text: “‘Dearest Senna. The rain continues. Have you attended a ball? Any ball?’”

introLines.speaker: SENNA
introLines.text: “‘Have you found someone who will put up with you?’”

introLines.speaker: SENNA
introLines.text: “She’s underlined *put up with*. Three times. She’s escalating.”

introLines.speaker: SENNA
introLines.text: “I’ll send her sixty-two sprains and a bee sting. That usually ends the correspondence for a month.”

introLines.speaker: NARRATOR
introLines.text: She picks up the next label. She doesn’t write anything on it.

introLines.speaker: SENNA
introLines.text: “Nobody sends home the person who knows where the burn salve is.”

introLines.speaker: SENNA
introLines.text: “So I always know where the burn salve is.”

introLines.speaker: SENNA
introLines.text: “An infirmary never runs out of sprains. There’s always a reason for me to be in the room.”

introLines.speaker: SENNA
introLines.text: “Without one, I’m a princess who skipped every ball and sniffs people’s tea. That takes some putting up with.”

introLines.speaker: NARRATOR
introLines.text: She ties off a jar with a knot that could moor a ship. She still hasn’t looked up.

options.labelText: “Sixty-two sprains? This palace would fall apart without you. Nobody’s sending you home.”

branchLines.speaker: SENNA
branchLines.text: “Yes. That’s the arrangement.”

branchLines.speaker: NARRATOR
branchLines.text: She hands you another bundle to sort, then a second before you’ve finished the first.

branchLines.speaker: SENNA
branchLines.text: “It’s kind. It’s also what I tell myself while I sweep.”

branchLines.speaker: NARRATOR
branchLines.text: When you leave, she’s sweeping a floor that was clean when you arrived.

options.internalLabel: Wrong; midpoint incomplete, no hearts changed

options.labelText: “If nobody in the palace ever sprained anything again, I’d still come and sit with you. Holding the twine badly.”

branchLines.speaker: NARRATOR
branchLines.text: Senna’s pencil stops in the middle of a word.

branchLines.speaker: SENNA
branchLines.text: “Badly.”

branchLines.speaker: PLAYER
branchLines.text: “Very badly. You’ve seen me with twine.”

branchLines.speaker: SENNA
branchLines.text: “I have. I nearly prescribed something.”

branchLines.speaker: NARRATOR
branchLines.text: She finishes the label and puts the jar on the shelf. Then she reads what she wrote.

branchLines.speaker: SENNA
branchLines.text: “I just labeled feverfew *feelings*. That’s your fault.”

branchLines.speaker: PLAYER
branchLines.text: “I can hold the lamp while you fix it.”

branchLines.speaker: SENNA
branchLines.text: “No. Leave it. I know what’s in it.”

branchLines.speaker: NARRATOR
branchLines.text: She reaches into the basket to find you something to do. Then she pushes the basket away.

branchLines.speaker: SENNA
branchLines.text: “Sit. Don’t hold anything. Don’t eat the soap.”

branchLines.speaker: NARRATOR
branchLines.text: You sit. She labels four more jars, all of them correctly. Pim snores through every one.

options.internalLabel: Correct; milestone completes, no hearts gained

options.labelText: “Give me her address. I’ll write and tell her exactly how much this court relies on you.”

branchLines.speaker: SENNA
branchLines.text: “You’d write to my mother.”

branchLines.speaker: PLAYER
branchLines.text: “Someone should tell her what you do here.”

branchLines.speaker: SENNA
branchLines.text: “She’ll write back. To you. With a list of every ball I’ve missed.”

branchLines.speaker: SENNA
branchLines.text: “I read you the letter. I didn’t ask anyone to answer it.”

branchLines.speaker: NARRATOR
branchLines.text: She takes the twine back and ties off the last jar herself. The knot is very tight.

options.internalLabel: Wrong; midpoint incomplete, no hearts changed

meta.Eligibility: Current Senna route; five committed hearts; midpoint incomplete; intelligence ≥ 6 and kindness ≥ 4.

meta.Objective: See her as wanted, not only needed: you would keep her company even if nobody were ever ill again.

introLines.speaker: NARRATOR
introLines.text: Senna sniffs a cup of something hot and holds it up to the light. Then she hands it to you.

introLines.speaker: SENNA
introLines.text: “Mint. Only mint. I checked twice.”

introLines.speaker: SENNA
introLines.text: “About the other day.”

introLines.speaker: NARRATOR
introLines.text: She finds her spectacles on her head on the first try. It seems to unsettle her.

introLines.speaker: SENNA
introLines.text: “You said something kind. I’ve tried it in three jars. It doesn’t fit any of them.”

options.labelText: “You work too hard. Take a day off and let someone else mind the infirmary for a while.”

branchLines.speaker: SENNA
branchLines.text: “A day off.”

branchLines.speaker: SENNA
branchLines.text: “Doctor Leeches says that too. He also says leeches.”

branchLines.speaker: NARRATOR
branchLines.text: She takes the cup back and rinses it, though it was clean. Then she says goodbye.

options.internalLabel: Wrong; milestone remains pending, no hearts changed

options.labelText: “I said it wrong. I like your company. Sprains optional.”

branchLines.speaker: SENNA
branchLines.text: “Sprains optional.”

branchLines.speaker: PLAYER
branchLines.text: “Discouraged, even.”

branchLines.speaker: SENNA
branchLines.text: “Good. I’m low on arnica.”

branchLines.speaker: NARRATOR
branchLines.text: She opens her notebook to a clean page and writes a heading: *Visitors*. Under it goes one name, underlined twice.

options.internalLabel: Correct; complete milestone, no hearts gained

meta.Type: mandatory midpoint retry; repeatable after a failed first attempt.
meta.Location: Senna's scheduled location.
meta.Objective: Say it plainly this time: you like her company, with or without anything to treat.
meta.END: One slot and one daily encounter, one journal entry, zero heart change; never replay the full midpoint.

introLines.speaker: NARRATOR
introLines.text: A grateful patient has given Senna a pastry. She breaks it in half and holds both halves up to the light.

introLines.speaker: SENNA
introLines.text: “Don’t eat that.”

introLines.speaker: PLAYER
introLines.text: “You haven’t given it to me.”

introLines.speaker: SENNA
introLines.text: “Preemptively. Don’t.”

introLines.speaker: NARRATOR
introLines.text: Out comes the magnifying lens. She questions a single currant until it has nothing left to say.

introLines.speaker: SENNA
introLines.text: “Butter. Currants. Something the baker is calling cinnamon.”

options.labelText: “What’s he calling cinnamon, then? I’ll wait for the full report.”

branchLines.speaker: SENNA
branchLines.text: “Nutmeg. A big enough dose makes you very ill. This is a festive dose.”

branchLines.speaker: NARRATOR
branchLines.text: She hands you the bigger half. You can tell she checked that too.

options.labelText: “I’ll try mine first. If I’m fine, you’re fine.”

branchLines.speaker: NARRATOR
branchLines.text: You eat your half before she can stop you.

branchLines.speaker: SENNA
branchLines.text: “A study with one participant. Terrible science. I’m not telling you the result.”

options.labelText: “That’s cinnamon. I can smell it from here.”

branchLines.speaker: SENNA
branchLines.text: “It’s nutmeg. The cinnamon is a rumor.”

branchLines.speaker: NARRATOR
branchLines.text: She hands you the smaller half.

introLines.speaker: NARRATOR
introLines.text: Senna sits down beside you and folds her hands in her lap. They stay there for almost a minute.

introLines.speaker: NARRATOR
introLines.text: Then the left one drifts toward the pocket labeled *twine*. She puts it back.

introLines.speaker: SENNA
introLines.text: “I’m practicing sitting. Without sorting anything.”

introLines.speaker: SENNA
introLines.text: “So far it’s harder than getting Pim to take his cough syrup.”

introLines.speaker: SENNA
introLines.text: “Stay if you like. No talking. That’s the whole prescription.”

options.labelText: “Want a distraction? I could tell you how I once fixed a printer by yelling at it.”

branchLines.speaker: SENNA
branchLines.text: “What’s a printer?”

branchLines.speaker: NARRATOR
branchLines.text: You explain. It takes a while. By the end, all her twine is sorted by length.

options.labelText: “Give me the hand that keeps wandering. I’ll keep it out of the twine.”

branchLines.speaker: NARRATOR
branchLines.text: She studies your hand like a sample of unknown origin. Then she puts hers in it.

branchLines.speaker: NARRATOR
branchLines.text: Nothing else happens for a good while. The twine stays in its pocket.

branchLines.speaker: SENNA
branchLines.text: “Pulse elevated. Mine. That’s not going in the notes.”

meta.END: Show exactly the selected branch, then resolve one encounter. Apply exactly one net heart change.

introLines.speaker: NARRATOR
introLines.text: Senna is searching her apron one labeled pocket at a time. She reaches *sweets, for patients* and stops.

introLines.speaker: SENNA
introLines.text: “My spectacles. I put them somewhere safe. I remember being very pleased with myself.”

introLines.speaker: NARRATOR
introLines.text: Something small and wire-framed is perched on top of your head.

introLines.speaker: PLAYER
introLines.text: “Senna. Look up.”

introLines.speaker: SENNA
introLines.text: “Oh. Yes. I put them on you. You were the only thing nearby that wasn’t going anywhere.”

options.labelText: “How do you lose things on your own head? Or, apparently, mine?”

branchLines.speaker: SENNA
branchLines.text: “Practice.”

branchLines.speaker: NARRATOR
branchLines.text: She lifts them off your head and leaves. Your head feels noticeably colder.

options.labelText: “Here. Maybe pick one place for them and always use it?”

branchLines.speaker: SENNA
branchLines.text: “One place. Yes. I did pick one.”

branchLines.speaker: NARRATOR
branchLines.text: She pushes them up onto her own head, where she’ll lose them again before you’ve finished talking.

options.labelText: “Leave them with me. I’ll guard them.”

branchLines.speaker: SENNA
branchLines.text: “Good. Don’t lean forward.”

branchLines.speaker: NARRATOR
branchLines.text: She goes back to her notes. Every so often she borrows them to read one line, then puts them back on your head.

meta.END: Show exactly the selected branch, then resolve one encounter. Apply exactly one net heart change.

introLines.speaker: NARRATOR
introLines.text: Mid-sentence, Senna takes your wrist and starts counting under her breath.

introLines.speaker: PLAYER
introLines.text: “Am I dying?”

introLines.speaker: SENNA
introLines.text: “Not of this. Don’t talk. You’ll skew it.”

introLines.speaker: SENNA
introLines.text: “Elevated. Either you like me or you took the stairs.”

introLines.speaker: NARRATOR
introLines.text: She waits with her pencil out, as if each answer goes in a different column.

options.labelText: “The stairs. Definitely the stairs. They were very steep.”

branchLines.speaker: SENNA
branchLines.text: “You haven’t moved in ten minutes.”

branchLines.speaker: SENNA
branchLines.text: “Hm. Disappointing.”

branchLines.speaker: NARRATOR
branchLines.text: She writes *stairs* in her notebook, followed by a small, pointed question mark.

options.labelText: “Both. Mostly the first.”

branchLines.speaker: SENNA
branchLines.text: “Mostly the first.”

branchLines.speaker: NARRATOR
branchLines.text: She lets go of your wrist and takes her own pulse instead. She doesn’t tell you the number.

branchLines.speaker: SENNA
branchLines.text: “It’s fine. It’s the stairs.”

meta.Pool: first-use fixed sequence; **stage:** post; **locale:** scheduled location only; **cost:** one slot and the daily encounter
meta.END: Show exactly the selected branch, then resolve one encounter. Apply exactly one net heart change.

introLines.speaker: SENNA
introLines.text: “I’ve been experiencing a deficiency.”

introLines.speaker: PLAYER
introLines.text: “Iron?”

introLines.speaker: SENNA
introLines.text: “You. Onset was the moment you left last time.”

introLines.speaker: SENNA
introLines.text: “Symptoms. I look up whenever anyone walks toward me. Fourteen times so far. Twelve were Pim.”

introLines.speaker: SENNA
introLines.text: “One was a goose. I don’t want to discuss the goose.”

introLines.speaker: NARRATOR
introLines.text: She opens her notebook to a page headed *Treatment* and waits, pencil ready.

options.labelText: “Same here. I kept turning to tell you things, and you weren’t there.”

branchLines.speaker: SENNA
branchLines.text: “Mutual.”

branchLines.speaker: NARRATOR
branchLines.text: Under *Treatment* she writes *Frequent doses.* She looks at it, crosses out *Frequent*, and writes *Daily.*

branchLines.speaker: SENNA
branchLines.text: “Now tell me the things. Oldest first.”

options.labelText: “Have you tried leeches? I hear Doctor Leeches swears by them.”

branchLines.speaker: SENNA
branchLines.text: “He’d prescribe six and a brisk walk.”

branchLines.speaker: NARRATOR
branchLines.text: She closes the notebook. The *Treatment* page stays blank.

introLines.speaker: NARRATOR
introLines.text: Royal Physician Dorrance approaches with his hat held humbly in both hands. It doesn’t suit him.

introLines.speaker: PHYSICIAN
introLines.text: “Your Highness. A purely academic question. A stable hand has a rash that four rounds of leeches have failed to improve.”

introLines.speaker: PHYSICIAN
introLines.text: “If anything, it has become offended.”

introLines.speaker: NARRATOR
introLines.text: Senna goes very still, like a cat that has just been handed the ribbon.

introLines.speaker: SENNA
introLines.text: “Doctor Leeches is asking me for help. Out loud. With witnesses.”

options.labelText: “Make him ask again in front of the whole court. He’s earned it.”

branchLines.speaker: SENNA
branchLines.text: “Nine seconds of satisfaction. Then he leeches the stable hand again, out of spite.”

branchLines.speaker: NARRATOR
branchLines.text: She gives Dorrance the answer in one flat sentence. He’s gone before she can enjoy any of it.

options.labelText: “You don’t owe him anything. Let him work it out himself.”

branchLines.speaker: SENNA
branchLines.text: “The stable hand would like him to work it out faster.”

branchLines.speaker: NARRATOR
branchLines.text: She tells Dorrance briskly, the way she’d hand back a glove he dropped.

options.labelText: “Help him. Then gloat to me afterward. In detail.”

branchLines.speaker: SENNA
branchLines.text: “New saddle soap. Change it. Stop the leeches. Mostly stop the leeches.”

branchLines.speaker: PHYSICIAN
branchLines.text: “The saddle soap. Of course. I was coming to that.”

branchLines.speaker: NARRATOR
branchLines.text: When he’s gone, she opens her notebook to a fresh page and writes *Gloating* across the top.

introLines.speaker: NARRATOR
introLines.text: Pim arrives at a run, waving a list. The handwriting gets bigger toward the bottom.

introLines.speaker: PIM
introLines.text: “Miss Senna, I want to learn medicine! Which plants are poison? Can I hold the foxglove? Are there needles?”

introLines.speaker: SENNA
introLines.text: “All of them, in the right amount. No. And there are no needles, Pim. There have never been needles.”

introLines.speaker: NARRATOR
introLines.text: She takes the list and folds it very small, the way she puts away anything with an edge.

introLines.speaker: SENNA
introLines.text: “He touches everything. Last week he licked a doorknob to find out what brass tastes like.”

options.labelText: “Maybe he’s a bit young for this? The stables might be safer for now.”

branchLines.speaker: SENNA
branchLines.text: “The stables. Where the horses kick.”

branchLines.speaker: NARRATOR
branchLines.text: Pim goes back anyway. Senna watches him the whole way, as if he might trip over the air.

options.labelText: “Start him somewhere safe. Who’s in charge of counting the boiled sweets?”

branchLines.speaker: SENNA
branchLines.text: “The sweets. Nothing in that bag can hurt him except the arithmetic.”

branchLines.speaker: PIM
branchLines.text: “Forty-one! Is that right? Is it a test? Did I pass?”

branchLines.speaker: SENNA
branchLines.text: “It’s forty. You’ve got one in your cheek. Write *forty*.”

options.labelText: “Why bother? He’s just a stable boy.”

branchLines.speaker: SENNA
branchLines.text: “He can name six plants you shouldn’t eat. You’ve tried to eat two of them.”

branchLines.speaker: NARRATOR
branchLines.text: She takes Pim by the sleeve and walks off, already explaining the first one.

introLines.speaker: NARRATOR
introLines.text: Senna unfolds a rota from her apron. Every hour is filled in, in very small handwriting.

introLines.speaker: SENNA
introLines.text: “I’ve made a change. Bottom line.”

introLines.speaker: NARRATOR
introLines.text: Under *Pim: sweets, bandages, no needles* is your name. Beside it: *Moral support.*

introLines.speaker: PLAYER
introLines.text: “I don’t know any medicine.”

introLines.speaker: SENNA
introLines.text: “Correct. That’s why you’re not on bandages.”

introLines.speaker: SENNA
introLines.text: “It’s a real post. Dorrance has one too. His says *Leeches (supervised).*”

options.labelText: “I accept. First job offer I’ve ever had. What are the duties?”

branchLines.speaker: SENNA
branchLines.text: “Sit within reach. Hand me things when I point. Sit within reach some more.”

branchLines.speaker: PLAYER
branchLines.text: “What’s the pay?”

branchLines.speaker: SENNA
branchLines.text: “One boiled sweet per shift. Don’t tell Pim. He’s on half.”

options.labelText: “Couldn’t we do something fun instead? You’re always working.”

branchLines.speaker: SENNA
branchLines.text: “Something fun. Instead.”

branchLines.speaker: NARRATOR
branchLines.text: She folds the rota back into her apron. Your name ends up on the inside of the fold.

introLines.speaker: NARRATOR
introLines.text: Senna presses a small paper packet into your hand. On the front, in her handwriting: *3 years.*

introLines.speaker: SENNA
introLines.text: “Seeds. It takes three years to flower. After that it flowers every year, if it likes you.”

introLines.speaker: PLAYER
introLines.text: “What is it?”

introLines.speaker: SENNA
introLines.text: “You’ll find out in three years.”

introLines.speaker: NARRATOR
introLines.text: She labels her own gloves *left* and *right*. This packet says *3 years* and nothing else.

introLines.speaker: SENNA
introLines.text: “I kept a packet for myself. That’s not relevant.”

options.labelText: “Three years? Have you got anything faster? I’m terrible at waiting.”

branchLines.speaker: SENNA
branchLines.text: “Cress. Four days.”

branchLines.speaker: SENNA
branchLines.text: “Very good in sandwiches.”

branchLines.speaker: NARRATOR
branchLines.text: She takes the packet back and tucks it into the pocket labeled *later*.

options.labelText: “How do I keep it alive for three years? Start from the beginning.”

branchLines.speaker: SENNA
branchLines.text: “From the beginning.”

branchLines.speaker: NARRATOR
branchLines.text: She talks for a long time. Frost. Slugs. Which slugs are friends. How to apologize to an overwatered seedling.

branchLines.speaker: SENNA
branchLines.text: “Year three is mostly waiting. I’ll check on it. On you. On it.”

introLines.speaker: NARRATOR
introLines.text: Someone has handed you a cup of tea. You lift it to drink, and Senna takes it out of your hands.

introLines.speaker: SENNA
introLines.text: “One moment.”

introLines.speaker: NARRATOR
introLines.text: She sniffs it. Then she dips a paper strip from her apron into it and squints at the strip.

introLines.speaker: SENNA
introLines.text: “Stewed. Four sugars. Whoever made this hates teeth.”

introLines.speaker: SENNA
introLines.text: “It’s safe. It’s also bad.”

introLines.speaker: SENNA
introLines.text: “I’ve smelled about four hundred cups of tea at this court. I’ve drunk none of them.”

options.labelText: “Thanks, but I can check my own tea.”

branchLines.speaker: SENNA
branchLines.text: “Noted.”

branchLines.speaker: NARRATOR
branchLines.text: She hands it back. You drink it. Four sugars is a lot of sugars.

options.labelText: “Want your own? You can smell it first. Twice, if you like.”

branchLines.speaker: SENNA
branchLines.text: “Mine?”

branchLines.speaker: NARRATOR
branchLines.text: You find her a cup. She inspects it for twice as long as yours, then drinks it.

branchLines.speaker: SENNA
branchLines.text: “Still bad. My face has gone warm. I’m blaming the tea.”

introLines.speaker: NARRATOR
introLines.text: Senna is patting down her apron pockets one at a time, in order.

introLines.speaker: SENNA
introLines.text: “Spectacles. I had them. I’m holding a seed the size of a comma, and I can’t see it.”

introLines.speaker: NARRATOR
introLines.text: She tries her magnifying lens on the seed, then gives the lens a look of betrayal.

introLines.speaker: SENNA
introLines.text: “I’ve retraced my steps. I’ve checked inside the herbal. Twice.”

introLines.speaker: NARRATOR
introLines.text: The spectacles are on top of her head, tucked in beside the pencil.

options.labelText: “Senna. Top of your head. Next to the pencil.”

branchLines.speaker: NARRATOR
branchLines.text: She reaches up and finds them. She puts them on, and you come into focus.

branchLines.speaker: SENNA
branchLines.text: “Huh. I had you down as blurrier.”

options.labelText: “I’ll help. Where did you last have them? Let’s retrace.”

branchLines.speaker: NARRATOR
branchLines.text: You help. Soon her entire apron is laid out in labeled rows.

branchLines.speaker: SENNA
branchLines.text: “Gone. I’ll have to identify the seed by smell.”

branchLines.speaker: NARRATOR
branchLines.text: From the top of her head, the spectacles have an excellent view of all this.

introLines.speaker: NARRATOR
introLines.text: Senna is restocking her apron. Every vial has a label. So does the ball of twine. It says *TWINE*.

introLines.speaker: NARRATOR
introLines.text: Then she takes out a small jar with a wax-sealed cork. Its label says *DO NOT*.

introLines.speaker: PLAYER
introLines.text: “Your label’s missing a verb.”

introLines.speaker: SENNA
introLines.text: “It’s missing all of them. On purpose.”

introLines.speaker: SENNA
introLines.text: “Whatever you were about to do with it, don’t.”

options.labelText: “I bet it’s the good sweets. Let me just have a peek.”

branchLines.speaker: SENNA
branchLines.text: “Don’t.”

branchLines.speaker: NARRATOR
branchLines.text: The jar goes into a pocket labeled *DEFINITELY DO NOT*. She buttons it.

options.labelText: “What’s in it? I’ll stand over here while you tell me.”

branchLines.speaker: SENNA
branchLines.text: “Rosary peas. *Abrus precatorius*. Bright red, with one black dot, like a ladybug keeping a secret.”

branchLines.speaker: SENNA
branchLines.text: “Someone was selling them strung as bracelets. Fine on a wrist. Chew one and you’d be very ill for a very long time.”

branchLines.speaker: NARRATOR
branchLines.text: She tilts the jar to show you the bottom. There’s a second label. It says *REALLY*.

introLines.speaker: NARRATOR
introLines.text: A courtier hurrying past presses a little tart into your hand. Three glossy red berries sit on top, around a spiky leaf.

introLines.speaker: NARRATOR
introLines.text: You get it halfway to your mouth. Then a gloved hand swats it out of your fingers.

introLines.speaker: SENNA
introLines.text: “Don’t eat that.”

introLines.speaker: NARRATOR
introLines.text: She picks the tart up by its very edge and holds it at arm’s length, like a specimen.

introLines.speaker: SENNA
introLines.text: “Holly. Lovely on a wreath. Terrible in a person.”

introLines.speaker: SENNA
introLines.text: “I’m Senna. Infirmary. You’d have met me in about an hour.”

options.labelText: “You saved my life! Thank you. Seriously, you’re incredible.”

branchLines.speaker: SENNA
branchLines.text: “I saved you two days in bed. Your life was never involved.”

branchLines.speaker: SENNA
branchLines.text: “Calm down. Be grateful at the correct size.”

options.labelText: “How could you tell from over there? It looked like a currant to me.”

branchLines.speaker: SENNA
branchLines.text: “Currants hang in strings. Holly sits in tight clumps, and every berry has a tiny black dot at the tip.”

branchLines.speaker: SENNA
branchLines.text: “Also, yours came with a leaf. Someone garnished your tart with a wreath.”

branchLines.speaker: NARRATOR
branchLines.text: She drops the berries into a vial labeled *NOT FOOD*. The vial is already half full.

options.labelText: “I knew. I was just seeing if you’d notice.”

branchLines.speaker: SENNA
branchLines.text: “Your mouth was open.”

branchLines.speaker: SENNA
branchLines.text: “Next time, test me with your mouth shut.”

introLines.speaker: NARRATOR
introLines.text: Senna is writing in the margin of a thick herbal. The crest on its cover belongs to the Royal Physician.

introLines.speaker: SENNA
introLines.text: “Page ninety. ‘For a burnt thumb, apply three leeches.’”

introLines.speaker: SENNA
introLines.text: “Three. On a thumb. I’ve written *cold water* and *leave the leeches out of this*.”

introLines.speaker: NARRATOR
introLines.text: A large man in velvet robes stops at her elbow. He looks at her pencil the way you’d look at a wasp.

introLines.speaker: PHYSICIAN
introLines.text: “Princess. That is *my* herbal. I have prescribed from that book for thirty years.”

introLines.speaker: SENNA
introLines.text: “I know, Doctor Leeches. I’ve met the thumbs.”

introLines.speaker: PHYSICIAN
introLines.text: “Dorrance. Doctor *Dorrance*.”

options.labelText: “Cold water for a burn. How long do you keep it under?”

branchLines.speaker: SENNA
branchLines.text: “Twenty minutes. Everyone stops at two and calls it twenty.”

branchLines.speaker: NARRATOR
branchLines.text: Dorrance sniffs. Then he takes out his own pencil and writes *twenty* beside her note.

branchLines.speaker: SENNA
branchLines.text: “By next week, that’ll have been his idea.”

options.labelText: “He’s the Royal Physician, though. Maybe go a little easier on him?”

branchLines.speaker: NARRATOR
branchLines.text: Senna rubs out *leave the leeches out of this*. She writes it again, smaller.

branchLines.speaker: SENNA
branchLines.text: “There. Easier.”

introLines.speaker: NARRATOR
introLines.text: Senna is peering at a knobbly brown root through her magnifying lens. She sniffs it, then sniffs it again.

introLines.speaker: PLAYER
introLines.text: “Lovely weather we’re having.”

introLines.speaker: SENNA
introLines.text: “Damp. Pressure dropping. By tomorrow, every knee over fifty will be forecasting rain.”

introLines.speaker: SENNA
introLines.text: “In Hollowmere, nobody discusses the weather. We treat it.”

introLines.speaker: NARRATOR
introLines.text: She sniffs the root a third time and writes something down.

options.labelText: “Think it’ll clear up, though?”

branchLines.speaker: SENNA
branchLines.text: “Prognosis: drizzle. Chronic.”

branchLines.speaker: NARRATOR
branchLines.text: She goes back to the root. You appear to have been discharged.

options.labelText: “Do you ever talk about anything normal?”

branchLines.speaker: SENNA
branchLines.text: “That was normal. You picked it.”

branchLines.speaker: NARRATOR
branchLines.text: She puts the root in a pocket and buttons the pocket shut.

options.labelText: “What is that? You’ve smelled it three times.”

branchLines.speaker: SENNA
branchLines.text: “Four. One was before you got here.”

branchLines.speaker: SENNA
branchLines.text: “*Valeriana officinalis*. Smells like a boot that’s been through something. Brew it and you sleep. Show it to a cat and the cat proposes.”

branchLines.speaker: NARRATOR
branchLines.text: She holds it out for you to sniff. It does smell like a boot.

introLines.speaker: NARRATOR
introLines.text: Pim, the infirmary’s young helper, runs up holding one hand as far from his face as it will go.

introLines.speaker: PIM
introLines.text: “A bee got me! The sting’s still in! Is a sting a needle? It’s a needle, isn’t it? Will you need a needle to get it out?”

introLines.speaker: SENNA
introLines.text: “Hand. It needs a fingernail and ten seconds.”

introLines.speaker: NARRATOR
introLines.text: She takes his wrist. Pim makes a noise like a kettle.

introLines.speaker: SENNA
introLines.text: “Look anywhere but your hand.”

introLines.speaker: PIM
introLines.text: “I can’t! It’s *my hand*!”

options.labelText: “It’s okay, Pim. You’re in very kind hands.”

branchLines.speaker: SENNA
branchLines.text: “Gloved hands. The dose is one sweet per sting. Two if there’s screaming.”

branchLines.speaker: NARRATOR
branchLines.text: She flicks the sting out. Pim, who watched every second of it, earns the second sweet.

options.labelText: “Pim, look at me. How big was this bee? Show me with your other hand.”

branchLines.speaker: PIM
branchLines.text: “This big! It had a *face*! It looked right at me, and then it…”

branchLines.speaker: SENNA
branchLines.text: “Done. Here. For patients.”

branchLines.speaker: PIM
branchLines.text: “A sweet! Wait. Did I miss the needle part?”

introLines.speaker: NARRATOR
introLines.text: Senna holds up two green sprigs, one in each gloved hand. They look like the same sprig, twice.

introLines.speaker: SENNA
introLines.text: “One’s parsley. The other is fool’s parsley.”

introLines.speaker: SENNA
introLines.text: “*Aethusa cynapium*. Named for its customers.”

introLines.speaker: SENNA
introLines.text: “Which one’s safe?”

introLines.speaker: NARRATOR
introLines.text: Neither sprig has a label. Everything else she carries has at least one.

options.labelText: “I have no idea. And I’m not eating either one.”

branchLines.speaker: SENNA
branchLines.text: “Correct.”

branchLines.speaker: SENNA
branchLines.text: “Everyone else guesses. The confident ones end up in my infirmary.”

branchLines.speaker: NARRATOR
branchLines.text: She ties a paper tag to each stem, humming. One says *PARSLEY*. The other says *DON’T*.

options.labelText: “That one. Flat leaves. That’s flat-leaf parsley, isn’t it?”

branchLines.speaker: SENNA
branchLines.text: “Fool’s parsley. Welcome, customer.”

branchLines.speaker: SENNA
branchLines.text: “They both have flat leaves. That’s the whole trick.”

branchLines.speaker: SENNA
branchLines.text: “You’d recover. I’d see to it. You wouldn’t enjoy how.”

introLines.speaker: NARRATOR
introLines.text: Senna is reading a letter sealed with green wax. She holds it at arm’s length, like a mushroom she doesn’t trust.

introLines.speaker: SENNA
introLines.text: “My mother. ‘Have you attended a ball? Are you presentable yet?’”

introLines.speaker: SENNA
introLines.text: “She underlined *presentable*. Twice. The nib went through.”

introLines.speaker: SENNA
introLines.text: “I looked it up. ‘Fit to be seen.’ I’m seen all day, mostly by people holding their own ankle.”

introLines.speaker: SENNA
introLines.text: “So what does she mean? Be specific.”

options.labelText: “Write back yes. Send her a sketch of you exactly like this. Apron and all.”

branchLines.speaker: SENNA
branchLines.text: “Apron and all.”

branchLines.speaker: NARRATOR
branchLines.text: She turns the letter over and writes: *Dear Mother. Yes. Sketch enclosed.*

branchLines.speaker: NARRATOR
branchLines.text: Then she pulls the pencil from her bun to start the sketch. The bun comes down. She draws that too.

options.labelText: “A princess with soil on her gloves? Your mother has a point.”

branchLines.speaker: SENNA
branchLines.text: “Then you two should write to each other.”

branchLines.speaker: NARRATOR
branchLines.text: She files the letter in an apron pocket labeled *IRRITANTS* and leaves.

options.labelText: “Maybe go to just one ball? It might make her happy.”

branchLines.speaker: SENNA
branchLines.text: “One ball.”

branchLines.speaker: SENNA
branchLines.text: “I could stand by the canapés and tell people which garnish to leave on the plate.”

branchLines.speaker: NARRATOR
branchLines.text: She writes *Considering it* on the back of the letter. She doesn’t underline anything.

introLines.speaker: NARRATOR
introLines.text: The Palace Court hosts a wedding for two people separately accused, with evidence, of talking too much.

introLines.speaker: TAVRI
introLines.text: “I’m told the guests expect a speech from the bride. As if they could stop one.”

introLines.speaker: PLAYER
introLines.text: “I brought a spare, in case.”

introLines.speaker: TAVRI
introLines.text: “Not the one with three key points?”

introLines.speaker: PLAYER
introLines.text: “New one. It’s called *In Case of Awkwardness, Break Glass.*”

introLines.speaker: TAVRI
introLines.text: “A bestseller.”

introLines.speaker: NARRATOR
introLines.text: When the guests settle, Tavri steps forward. Her tail gives one nervous swish.

introLines.speaker: TAVRI
introLines.text: “I had jokes ready. They were excellent. One of them had a goat in it.”

introLines.speaker: NARRATOR
introLines.text: She looks at the guests, then at you, and puts her notes away.

introLines.speaker: TAVRI
introLines.text: “I’m happy to be here, with the person I chose.”

introLines.speaker: NARRATOR
introLines.text: That’s the whole speech. She sits down looking extremely pleased with herself.

introLines.speaker: NARRATOR
introLines.text: Later, in the gardens, a gossip scroll flutters down. It claims the newlyweds plan to have fifty children.

introLines.speaker: PLAYER
introLines.text: “That’s a very specific rumor.”

introLines.speaker: TAVRI
introLines.text: “Let’s start smaller. One houseplant. See if it survives us.”

introLines.speaker: PLAYER
introLines.text: “Leave it with me. I’ll draw up a maintenance schedule.”

introLines.speaker: TAVRI
introLines.text: “I said yes to you without one. Look how well that’s going.”

introLines.speaker: NARRATOR
introLines.text: You buy a fern. It survives. The maintenance schedule does not.

introLines.speaker: NARRATOR
introLines.text: Someone in the Town Square has built a very small stage. A hand-painted sign reads *Royal Comedy Showcase: Participation Voluntary, Embarrassment Inevitable.*

introLines.speaker: TAVRI
introLines.text: “Finally, some honest advertising.”

introLines.speaker: PLAYER
introLines.text: “Are you going up?”

introLines.speaker: TAVRI
introLines.text: “I put my name down earlier. Now I’d rather be in the crowd, heckling.”

introLines.speaker: NARRATOR
introLines.text: Up front, a wizard pulls a rabbit from a hat.

introLines.speaker: NARRATOR
introLines.text: The rabbit takes one look at the audience and pulls the wizard back inside.

introLines.speaker: PLAYER
introLines.text: “Tough act to follow.”

introLines.speaker: TAVRI
introLines.text: “That rabbit has better instincts than I do.”

introLines.speaker: TAVRI
introLines.text: “The court expects me to be brilliant on command. Like a lamp.”

introLines.speaker: TAVRI
introLines.text: “I don’t want to be a lamp. I don’t want to disappoint everyone, either.”

introLines.speaker: PLAYER
introLines.text: “What do you actually want?”

introLines.speaker: TAVRI
introLines.text: “That’s becoming a dangerous question around you.”

introLines.speaker: NARRATOR
introLines.text: Her tail points at the stage, then at the crowd, then at you.

options.labelText: “Go up and I’ll cheer, badly. Stay and we’ll watch terrible jokes together. I’m here either way.”

branchLines.speaker: TAVRI
branchLines.text: “I think I’d like to stay. Just stay.”

branchLines.speaker: NARRATOR
branchLines.text: The next comedian announces that his act is entirely improvised.

branchLines.speaker: NARRATOR
branchLines.text: He unrolls a scroll labeled *Entirely Improvised Act* and starts reading.

branchLines.speaker: TAVRI
branchLines.text: “Look. Someone even less spontaneous than you.”

branchLines.speaker: PLAYER
branchLines.text: “That was spontaneous and hurtful.”

branchLines.speaker: TAVRI
branchLines.text: “And I didn’t even need the stage.”

options.labelText: “You’re brilliant at this. You’ll feel better the second you’re up there.”

branchLines.speaker: TAVRI
branchLines.text: “Maybe. I’d have liked to decide that myself.”

branchLines.speaker: NARRATOR
branchLines.text: She goes up and does ten tidy minutes. The crowd loves it.

branchLines.speaker: NARRATOR
branchLines.text: Coming back down, she thanks everyone. Her smile lasts almost to the bottom step.

options.labelText: “Backing out makes you look weak. A real princess wouldn’t let her public down.”

branchLines.speaker: TAVRI
branchLines.text: “Wonderful. A review, and I didn’t even go on.”

branchLines.speaker: NARRATOR
branchLines.text: She walks off into the crowd and doesn’t look back for you.

introLines.speaker: NARRATOR
introLines.text: A folded paper owl lands beside Tavri and hoots once. Then it unfolds itself into a glowing scroll.

introLines.speaker: TAVRI
introLines.text: “Ah. Fantasygram. This week’s public humiliation, delivered by express owl.”

introLines.speaker: PLAYER
introLines.text: “You’re on Fantasygram?”

introLines.speaker: TAVRI
introLines.text: “The palace has an account. I’m its public-relations emergency.”

introLines.speaker: NARRATOR
introLines.text: On the scroll, Tavri hurries away from a banquet table.

introLines.speaker: NARRATOR
introLines.text: The caption reads *Princess Flees Dinner After Losing Fight with Napkin.*

introLines.speaker: TAVRI
introLines.text: “I was helping a servant with a spilled tray! There was gravy on the ceiling!”

introLines.speaker: TAVRI
introLines.text: “They cropped out the servant. They cropped out the tray. They kept the napkin.”

introLines.speaker: PLAYER
introLines.text: “The crop tool. Most dangerous spell in the kingdom.”

introLines.speaker: TAVRI
introLines.text: “Finally, a scholar who understands modern sorcery. Point to you.”

introLines.speaker: NARRATOR
introLines.text: A second paper owl lands. Its scroll is titled *Ten Reasons the Princess Is Secretly Unfit for Polite Society.*

introLines.speaker: TAVRI
introLines.text: “Ten! Busy week. Number one’s the napkin, I assume. Number two, also the napkin.”

introLines.speaker: TAVRI
introLines.text: “Number three, ‘laughs like a goose.’ Fair. Number four—”

introLines.speaker: NARRATOR
introLines.text: She stops reading. Her tail has wrapped itself tight around her ankles.

introLines.speaker: TAVRI
introLines.text: “If I joke about it first, nobody notices it bothered me. That’s the usual plan.”

introLines.speaker: PLAYER
introLines.text: “How’s the plan going?”

introLines.speaker: TAVRI
introLines.text: “Badly. I’m out of napkin material. Your move.”

options.labelText: “Skip the joke. It’s a rotten scroll. Want to tell people the gravy story, or ignore it with me?”

branchLines.speaker: TAVRI
branchLines.text: “You’d let me pick? Even if it’s profoundly unprincesslike?”

branchLines.speaker: PLAYER
branchLines.text: “Especially then.”

branchLines.speaker: TAVRI
branchLines.text: “Then I’d like to put the scroll away and be upset for one minute.”

branchLines.speaker: NARRATOR
branchLines.text: She puts it away. You wait out the minute with her. Nobody says anything clever.

branchLines.speaker: NARRATOR
branchLines.text: Then the paper owl folds itself into a napkin. A visibly judgmental napkin.

branchLines.speaker: TAVRI
branchLines.text: “Oh, don’t *you* start.”

branchLines.speaker: NARRATOR
branchLines.text: She laughs at a napkin. Loudly. She doesn’t check who heard.

options.labelText: “It’s just gossip. Hit back with something funnier and everyone will forget it.”

branchLines.speaker: TAVRI
branchLines.text: “Something funnier. Yes. That’s what I normally do.”

branchLines.speaker: PLAYER
branchLines.text: “I was trying to help.”

branchLines.speaker: TAVRI
branchLines.text: “Of course you were. I was hoping for the other one.”

branchLines.speaker: NARRATOR
branchLines.text: She pockets the scroll. The joke she makes about it later is excellent.

options.labelText: “Maybe they’ve got a point. A competent princess wouldn’t give them material.”

branchLines.speaker: TAVRI
branchLines.text: “Oh.”

branchLines.speaker: TAVRI
branchLines.text: “Number eleven. Thank you. That saves them an owl.”

branchLines.speaker: NARRATOR
branchLines.text: She rolls up both scrolls and goes.

TAV-FIN-01.title: Shared Confession (first full final marriage scene)

introLines.speaker: NARRATOR
introLines.text: The conversation winds down to the sound of the fountain. Nobody rushes to fill the quiet.

introLines.speaker: TAVRI
introLines.text: “Careful. That’s your speech face.”

introLines.speaker: PLAYER
introLines.text: “I did prepare one. It might be a mistake.”

introLines.speaker: TAVRI
introLines.text: “A speech? For me? Is there a handout?”

introLines.speaker: PLAYER
introLines.text: “It has a beginning, three key points and a conclusion.”

introLines.speaker: TAVRI
introLines.text: “My heart trembles before your formatting.”

introLines.speaker: NARRATOR
introLines.text: You unfold the paper. Every tidy sentence on it looks like somewhere to hide.

introLines.speaker: PLAYER
introLines.text: “Actually… I don’t want to read it.”

introLines.speaker: TAVRI
introLines.text: “Take your time. Skip the clever bits. I’ve got plenty coming out of my ears.”

introLines.speaker: PLAYER
introLines.text: “I came here trying to become someone who could win a princess.”

introLines.speaker: PLAYER
introLines.text: “You kept showing me I didn’t need a perfect line to care about someone.”

introLines.speaker: TAVRI
introLines.text: “And you showed me someone can stay after the last joke.”

introLines.speaker: NARRATOR
introLines.text: Her tail flicks once. Then she waits.

options.labelText: “I love your clever lines, and the moments you run out of them. Will you marry me, and work out the rest as equals?”

branchLines.speaker: TAVRI
branchLines.text: “That was disastrously unscripted.”

branchLines.speaker: PLAYER
branchLines.text: “I know.”

branchLines.speaker: TAVRI
branchLines.text: “You didn’t promise I’d never be frightened again.”

branchLines.speaker: PLAYER
branchLines.text: “I couldn’t promise that honestly.”

branchLines.speaker: TAVRI
branchLines.text: “Good. I’d have asked for references.”

branchLines.speaker: NARRATOR
branchLines.text: She takes your hand.

branchLines.speaker: TAVRI
branchLines.text: “Yes, {PLAYER}. I choose you too.”

branchLines.speaker: TAVRI
branchLines.text: “That’s my whole speech. One point. No conclusion.”

branchLines.speaker: NARRATOR
branchLines.text: Your prepared speech slips off the edge of the fountain. Nobody fishes it out.

options.internalLabel: Correct; terminal success and gallery unlock

options.labelText: “Marry me, and I’ll make sure you’re always everyone’s favorite princess. Nobody will ever be disappointed in you.”

branchLines.speaker: TAVRI
branchLines.text: “That’s a lovely-sounding cage.”

branchLines.speaker: PLAYER
branchLines.text: “I wanted to make you happy.”

branchLines.speaker: TAVRI
branchLines.text: “Then listen. I don’t want to be a flawless princess in your care. I want to be a person beside you.”

branchLines.speaker: NARRATOR
branchLines.text: She doesn’t walk away. She doesn’t say yes, either.

options.internalLabel: Wrong; no new heart penalty; marriage retry pending at ten hearts

options.labelText: “Say yes and we’ll be the funniest royal couple in history. Imagine the applause.”

branchLines.speaker: TAVRI
branchLines.text: “I can imagine it. I can also imagine us as strangers the minute the curtain falls.”

branchLines.speaker: TAVRI
branchLines.text: “Ask me because you want a life with me. Not a double act.”

options.internalLabel: Wrong; no new heart penalty; marriage retry pending at ten hearts

TAV-MID-01.title: The Private Confession (first full midpoint attempt)

introLines.speaker: NARRATOR
introLines.text: Tavri walks with you until the noise of the court is behind a hedge.

introLines.speaker: NARRATOR
introLines.text: The Royal Gardens are so quiet you can hear the fountain hiccup.

introLines.speaker: TAVRI
introLines.text: “Congratulations. You’ve been granted my exclusive, invitation-only silence. Reviews are mixed.”

introLines.speaker: PLAYER
introLines.text: “Should I clap?”

introLines.speaker: TAVRI
introLines.text: “Please don’t. I’ve been clapped at enough for one lifetime.”

introLines.speaker: NARRATOR
introLines.text: She sits on the edge of the fountain. Her tail, which never stops, stops.

introLines.speaker: TAVRI
introLines.text: “Do you know what happens when you’re the funny princess?”

introLines.speaker: TAVRI
introLines.text: “Nobody asks if you’re all right. They ask when you’ll be funny again.”

introLines.speaker: PLAYER
introLines.text: “That sounds lonely.”

introLines.speaker: TAVRI
introLines.text: “It’s comfortable, as long as you never stop.”

introLines.speaker: TAVRI
introLines.text: “I can make a whole court laugh. I once made a tax collector laugh. During an audit.”

introLines.speaker: TAVRI
introLines.text: “And I don’t know if anyone would stay if I ran out of clever things to say.”

introLines.speaker: NARRATOR
introLines.text: She waits for the joke that usually comes next. It doesn’t come.

options.labelText: “Can I tell you something? I hide behind being useful.”

branchLines.speaker: PLAYER
branchLines.text: “Before I came here, I got turned down for job after job. I kept thinking that if I was useful enough, I’d finally earn a place.”

branchLines.speaker: PLAYER
branchLines.text: “When I’m not succeeding at something, I don’t know who I am.”

branchLines.speaker: PLAYER
branchLines.text: “But I’d sit here with you even if neither of us said anything clever.”

branchLines.speaker: TAVRI
branchLines.text: “You? You explain disasters as tidy little lists.”

branchLines.speaker: PLAYER
branchLines.text: “The lists are how you know I’m panicking.”

branchLines.speaker: TAVRI
branchLines.text: “That’s an alarming amount of honesty for one fountain.”

branchLines.speaker: PLAYER
branchLines.text: “We can stop.”

branchLines.speaker: TAVRI
branchLines.text: “No. I want to try something.”

branchLines.speaker: TAVRI
branchLines.text: “I had a miserable day.”

branchLines.speaker: NARRATOR
branchLines.text: Nothing sparkles after it. She looks startled that she let the sentence out unsupervised.

branchLines.speaker: PLAYER
branchLines.text: “I’m sorry. Want to tell me about it?”

branchLines.speaker: TAVRI
branchLines.text: “Only if you promise not to file a quarterly report on my feelings.”

branchLines.speaker: NARRATOR
branchLines.text: She tells you about it. None of it is funny.

branchLines.speaker: NARRATOR
branchLines.text: Somewhere around the part with the soup, her tail starts moving again.

options.internalLabel: Correct; milestone completes, no hearts gained

options.labelText: “That’s ridiculous. Everyone adores you. You’re the funniest person in the kingdom.”

branchLines.speaker: TAVRI
branchLines.text: “Yes. That’s the part I’m worried about.”

branchLines.speaker: PLAYER
branchLines.text: “I meant it kindly.”

branchLines.speaker: TAVRI
branchLines.text: “Oh, I know you did.”

branchLines.speaker: TAVRI
branchLines.text: “Anyway! Have I told you about the duke and the soup?”

branchLines.speaker: NARRATOR
branchLines.text: Her tail is moving again, a little too fast.

options.internalLabel: Wrong; midpoint incomplete, no hearts changed

options.labelText: “Then we make sure you never run out. I’ll help you write new material.”

branchLines.speaker: TAVRI
branchLines.text: “I asked if you’d stay when the jokes run out. You offered to improve the show.”

branchLines.speaker: PLAYER
branchLines.text: “That wasn’t what you were asking.”

branchLines.speaker: TAVRI
branchLines.text: “No.”

branchLines.speaker: NARRATOR
branchLines.text: She stands, brushes herself off, and is charming all the way back past the hedge.

options.internalLabel: Wrong; midpoint incomplete, no hearts changed

introLines.speaker: TAVRI

branchLines.speaker: NARRATOR
branchLines.text: She walks past the sign. The joke stays where it is, unspent.

branchLines.text: She looks delighted for exactly as long as it takes to find the nap spot.

branchLines.speaker: TAVRI

introLines.text: “What about the kings?”

branchLines.text: You stand in it. It is, as reported, nice.

branchLines.speaker: TAVRI

branchLines.speaker: NARRATOR

help.title: First Steps
help.text: You have 28 days in the royal courtship season. Each day has morning, afternoon, and evening. A valid action uses one slot; looking at menus and Help does not. Select the princess whose story you want to pursue.

help.title: Finding Her
help.text: The princesses have different repeating weekly schedules. Check the calendar before attempting a conversation. An unavailable meeting cannot become an extra visit.

help.title: One Conversation
help.text: You can speak to your selected princess once on an eligible day. A conversation uses one slot even when you choose an answer she dislikes.

help.title: Training Basics
help.text: Your four stats are Charisma, Intelligence, Strength, and Kindness. There are two approved training activities for each. Levels one through five require one training session each; levels six through ten require two sessions each.

help.title: Five Hearts
help.text: Five hearts is an intentional story gate, not a broken meter. Once your requirements are met, the next eligible princess encounter brings a pivotal conversation. The requirements panel shows what is missing.

help.title: Preparation Needed
help.text: The next pivotal conversation is waiting for preparation. Check the visible primary and secondary stat requirements and train as needed. Looking at this notice costs no slot.

help.title: Try Again Later
help.text: That was a consequential answer, not a command error. The midpoint did not complete; hearts were not additionally penalized. Another eligible day offers the shorter follow-up.

help.title: Ten Hearts
help.text: An ordinary or optional encounter that reaches ten hearts continues directly into the approved proposal scene. It is part of the same encounter, not a new day or extra slot.

help.title: A Better Proposal
help.text: An unsuccessful proposal leaves your relationship at ten hearts and a later-day follow-up pending. Keep an eye on the remaining calendar.

help.title: Last Days
help.text: The 28-day deadline is real. Resolve any pending milestone or proposal while you still have an eligible scheduled encounter. The last evening is playable; there is no playable Day 29.

help.title: Unexpected Moments
help.text: Some princess moments are optional and can be missed. Explore naturally; you do not need every optional story to reach marriage.

help.title: Saving Progress
help.text: The game keeps local progress and offers explicit backup/export and recovery options. Read the displayed save status before leaving. If saving reports a problem, use the recovery guidance without assuming the progress was safely stored.

help.title: Recovering a Save
help.text: If a backup import or recovery fails, do not overwrite a working save merely to retry. Read the validation error and choose the recovery option that preserves the most reliable existing state.

help.title: After the Deadline
help.text: A failed courtship ends the run, but the journal remains available until you explicitly confirm a new start. Losing does not silently erase the record of your choices.

squareQuips.speaker: HUMPTY

squareQuips.speaker: HUMPTY
squareQuips.text: “People call me difficult to put back together. The glue merchants call me a valued long-term customer.”

squareQuips.speaker: HUMPTY
squareQuips.text: “A locked milestone is not an angry princess. The milestone is a number. The princess will tell you exactly what you did.”

squareQuips.speaker: HUMPTY
squareQuips.text: “In an important conversation, the cleverest thing you can say is often a question. I have many questions. Most of them are about walls.”

squareQuips.speaker: HUMPTY
squareQuips.text: “My advice is free. The premium package is the same advice, delivered from a lower wall.”

squareQuips.speaker: HUMPTY
squareQuips.text: “The palace believes every problem needs a committee. I believe every problem needs a chair. Low to the ground. With arms.”

squareQuips.speaker: HUMPTY
squareQuips.text: “When a mermaid tells you the water is where she belongs, believe the expert. I feel the same way about the ground.”

squareQuips.speaker: HUMPTY
squareQuips.text: “A dragon princess can open her own doors, and most walls. You may still ask whether she would like company.”

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: You read a chapter called “Openers for Royalty.” Opener four is just winking. You close the book before it can suggest opener five.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: You practice a line on the mirror. The mirror loves it. The mirror is not a princess.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: You chat with the townsfolk. One question to a baker earns you twenty minutes on sourdough and a free roll.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: Nobody grades you. Several people ask your name. Progress.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: You read two histories of the same obscure custom. They disagree about everything, including the custom.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: You leave with one answer and three better questions. The librarian calls this a good day.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: The oracle answers instantly, with great confidence and three footnotes. Two of the footnotes cite the oracle. You check the sources.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: Asked to show its work, the oracle concedes that “probably” was doing most of it.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: You work through a careful set of push-ups and squats. Form over noise. Mostly.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: The floor survives another session. So, narrowly, do you.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: You run drills on the guild’s ordinary equipment. A veteran watches, says “Hm,” and leaves. You decide that was praise.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: The training dummy remains intact. The guild counts this as a win for everyone, including the dummy.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: You refill the water bowls and find the garden dogs some shade. One of them sits on your foot so you can’t leave.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: The reviews are in: one wagging tail, one sneeze, no numbers.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: You pick up litter around the square. The flowerbeds look better. A pigeon looks betrayed.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: Nobody throws you a parade. Given what parades leave behind, that’s for the best.
